{{hero}} covered an auctioneer moving the jar toward a cooler. Shots broke a gallery lamp, and the fighter answered as the auctioneer found a second seed inside the jar’s lid. One was green, the other black; the note in the loading bay mentioned only the green one.

The detail could secure both seeds in the auction room or take the green one to the bay to learn who sent the note. The researchers had a test kit ready, but it would consume part of a seed. The fighter watched the cooler close around the jar while footsteps approached outside the bay.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s detail secured both seeds and identified the missing buyer.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s researchers kept the samples and began testing their effect on the blight.
endings.draw: The seeds remained untouched while both teams held the auction hall through the night.

paragraphs: A hospital’s ambulance garage lost heat during a rare night freeze. Its vehicles were ready to leave, but the entrance shutter had iced into its tracks. {{heroPlayer}}’s hired guards took the garage floor; {{otherPlayer}}’s clinic staff held the boiler room and brought a trolley of heated water.

{{hero}} wrestled a defender at the shutter crank and forced it to turn a fraction. The fighter held it as a mechanic poured the hot water along the frozen rail. A crack sounded above the garage door; the shutter moved, but a loose support pin began dropping toward the first ambulance’s roof.

The guards could lift the shutter quickly and move the ambulances, risking the falling pin, or stop to replace it while a call waited outside the clinic. The staff had a spare support in the boiler room. The fighter kept the crank steady as the driver started the first engine.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s guards freed the garage and sent the ambulance safely to its call.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s staff secured the shutter and brought the vehicles out under its own direction.
endings.draw: The ambulance left, but both parties kept the garage closed until its rail was rebuilt.

paragraphs: A telescope on a clinic roof was meant to guide night couriers across the desert. It started pointing to a distant hill after the route there had been closed. {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians reached the roof controls; {{otherPlayer}}’s medical couriers guarded the stairs while one delivery remained on the road.

{{hero}} opened the tracking unit and found a small mirror installed behind its lens. The specialist moved it aside, restoring the safe route, then saw a light on the closed hill answering the telescope’s beam. A courier on the road called that someone was signaling from the wrong direction.

The technicians could keep the telescope on the safe route or turn it briefly to learn who was on the hill. The medical couriers had a ground beacon ready for the delivery. The specialist held the mirror against the roof rail as the distant light blinked a request to wait.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians guided the delivery safely and traced the light on the hill.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s couriers secured the stairs and marked the road with their beacon.
endings.draw: The medicine arrived, but both parties left the hill’s unexpected signal unanswered.

paragraphs: A remote research station’s fence alarm sounded although its gates remained shut. Inside, a botanist had reported a missing tray of test plants. {{heroPlayer}}’s guards took the perimeter road; {{otherPlayer}}’s medical team held the laboratory and checked whether the plants had been carried through a service drain.

{{hero}} covered a worker inspecting the fence. Fire struck a post beside the gate, and the fighter answered while the worker found a loose panel large enough for a tray. Beyond it lay fresh footprints toward an abandoned watch hut, with a green leaf caught under one boot mark.

The guards could follow the tracks and leave the fence open, or secure the panel before more trays disappeared. The medical team had a carrier case ready for the plants if found. The fighter watched the watch hut’s window brighten in the fading light as the worker held up the trapped leaf.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s guards recovered the tray and secured the station fence.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s team held the laboratory and brought the plants back from the watch hut.
endings.draw: The fence was repaired, but neither team found the missing tray before nightfall.

paragraphs: Two investigators followed the same missing courier to an empty music hall. The courier had left one sealed letter on the stage and another beneath the balcony rail. {{heroPlayer}}’s team entered through the orchestra door; {{otherPlayer}}’s party held the upper gallery, each unsure which letter was meant for them.

{{hero}} met a defender at the steep gallery stairs and fought for room to reach the second letter. The fighter caught it before a draft carried it over the rail. Inside was a ticket for tomorrow’s performance with a seat circled beside the hall’s locked service hatch.

The investigators could open the hatch tonight and risk losing the courier’s trail outside, or wait for the performance and watch the circled seat. The other team had the stage letter still sealed. The fighter held the ticket as a note sounded from the dark orchestra pit.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s team found the courier and secured the hall’s hidden route.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s party opened the stage letter and reached the courier first.
endings.draw: Both letters survived, but the courier stayed missing when the hall lights came back on.

paragraphs: A ferry crossing under quarantine received a passenger manifest with one name written twice. The second entry listed a berth beneath the deck where no cabin existed. {{heroPlayer}}’s port inspectors checked the gangway; {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators guarded the sealed luggage while the ferryman kept everyone aboard.

{{hero}} traced the duplicate berth to a hatch hidden below the ticket booth. The specialist lifted it and found a small compartment holding a clean change of clothes and a note addressed to the duplicated passenger. Water was seeping through the floorboards as the ferry pulled against its mooring.

The inspectors could open the compartment fully and look for the passenger, but the ferry might flood if its lower seal broke. The investigators had a rope at the luggage end and asked for the note. The specialist held the hatch as a voice from beneath the deck answered the duplicated name.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s inspectors found the passenger and secured the ferry’s hidden compartment.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators took the gangway and brought the passenger out from below.
endings.draw: The ferry stayed afloat, but both teams held the disputed manifest until everyone was counted.

paragraphs: A temporary relief bridge crossed a dry riverbed outside a field clinic. In the afternoon heat, its metal joints expanded and the center span bowed over a line of patients waiting to cross. {{heroPlayer}}’s medics reached the near abutment; {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators held the far side where the bridge plans were stored.

{{hero}} checked the joints and found one brace fitted in reverse. The specialist eased its bolt loose, straightening the span for a moment. A groan came from the opposite abutment as the load shifted toward the waiting patients’ route, and a worker called for the original drawing.

The medics could clear the queue and close the bridge, delaying care, or brace the far joint while patients crossed one at a time. The investigators had the drawing and a shorter footpath nearby. The specialist held the loose bolt as the first patient stepped onto the cooling metal.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s medics stabilized the span and brought the patients across for care.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators secured the far side and guided the patients by the footpath.
endings.draw: The patients reached the clinic, but both teams closed the bridge until its brace was corrected.

paragraphs: An abandoned courier warehouse began receiving drones addressed to people who no longer lived in the district. The latest package carried an address for the building itself. {{heroPlayer}}’s signal crew came through the loading yard; {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators watched the roof vent where the drones disappeared.

{{hero}} covered a technician reaching the conveyor controls. Shots struck the warehouse shutters, and the fighter answered while the technician caught the newest package. Inside was a key to a parcel locker beneath the floor, and the conveyor had begun moving toward a door the warehouse plans did not show.

The crew could stop the conveyor and open the locker or let the package travel to its intended recipient. The investigators had found a narrow stair behind the roof vent. The fighter watched the key turn in the technician’s hand as a fresh drone landed on the moving belt.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew secured the conveyor and traced the packages to their hidden destination.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators took the warehouse and opened the locker from the hidden stair.
endings.draw: The packages stopped arriving, but both teams kept the unexplained door under watch.

paragraphs: A rehearsal stage kept lowering its curtain during the final act, even after its machinery was unplugged. The performers found a note pinned backstage naming a missing member of the company. {{heroPlayer}}’s stage crew entered through the prop room; {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators guarded the audience aisle where the missing person had last been seen.

{{hero}} fought a defender at the narrow fly-rail and kept the curtain rope from slipping through their hands. As the fighter secured it, a hidden trap opened below the stage. A light shone into the space, revealing a coat with the missing performer’s name sewn into its lining.

The crew could descend through the trap, but the curtain would fall unless someone held the rope. The investigators had another route through the orchestra pit. The fighter heard footsteps below as the performers stopped speaking and the theater fell quiet around the still-open hatch.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew held the stage and found the missing performer beneath it.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators secured the orchestra pit and brought the performer out.
endings.draw: The coat was recovered, but both teams kept searching after the footsteps faded.

paragraphs: A cargo crane above a river terminal lifted an empty container that began tapping from within. Its manifest listed a shipment delivered a week earlier, though nobody at the terminal remembered unloading it. {{heroPlayer}}’s riggers reached the crane platform; {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators held the terminal office with the original delivery papers.

{{hero}} covered a welder crossing to the suspended container. Fire struck the platform railing, and the fighter answered while the welder cut through its seal. Inside was a radio playing a message recorded in the terminal office, and beneath it a fresh bootprint in the otherwise empty floor.

The container could be brought down for inspection, but its swaying load hung directly over the office. The investigators offered a safe landing space on the far dock. The fighter watched the welder clip in a guide line as the radio repeated a warning about the crane’s next lift.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s riggers landed the container and traced its unexplained recording.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators secured the far dock and matched the recording to its source.
endings.draw: The container landed safely, but no one could explain the fresh print inside.

paragraphs: A private archive released the same sealed identity file to two separate requesters, each claiming to be its subject. The original had been locked in an escrow cabinet since childhood. {{heroPlayer}}’s auditors took the reading desk; {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators held the side door where one requester had been told to wait.

{{hero}} compared the copies and found a faint watermark missing from both. The specialist opened the cabinet to find its original still intact, with a fresh handwritten page tucked inside. The page named a third person and gave the time of an appointment at the archive’s back window that afternoon.

The auditors could verify the original now or watch the window to learn who arranged the copies. The investigators had a clear line to the back courtyard. The specialist held the original beneath the desk lamp as someone outside knocked three times against the glass.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s auditors secured the original and identified who made the false copies.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators took the courtyard and met the third requester.
endings.draw: All three files remained under seal while the claimants waited for a hearing.

paragraphs: A navigation beacon on a salt flat began naming every person who approached it, then repeated a name nobody recognized. The old survey team had left no log of installing it. {{heroPlayer}}’s searchers came along the raised track; {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators held the beacon hut and asked for its memory core.

{{hero}} covered a technician crossing the open salt. Fire struck a metal mast, and the fighter answered while the technician found a recording cylinder below the beacon. The unknown name was etched on its lid. Inside, the cylinder carried a route to a second hut standing beyond the edge of the mapped flat.

The technician could remove the cylinder or leave it spinning while the searchers followed the route. The investigators had a faster approach to the unmapped hut from the far side. The fighter heard the beacon repeat the unknown name again as a lamp lit in the distance.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s searchers held the beacon and reached the second hut with the cylinder intact.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators secured the core and followed the distant lamp.
endings.draw: The light went out before either party reached it, leaving the name unexplained.

paragraphs: An old fort’s cistern began filling with warm water despite a month without rain. The garrison feared a pipe beneath its cellar had been opened from outside. {{heroPlayer}}’s expedition came to the courtyard; {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators held the cellar door with a drawing of the forgotten pipe network.

{{hero}} struggled with a defender at the cistern hatch and forced room for an engineer to look inside. A sealed message cylinder floated against the grate, its wax impressed with the fort’s own mark. As the engineer reached for it, the waterline climbed over a second opening in the stone.

The expedition could pull out the message and close the hatch or open the second passage before it flooded. The investigators had a dry stair to the lower pipe, but needed the courtyard gate. The fighter held the hatch as a hollow knock sounded through the rising water.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s expedition secured the cistern and recovered the message without flooding the fort.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators took the lower pipe and traced the water to its source.
endings.draw: The message survived, but both groups sealed the flooded passage for a later search.

paragraphs: A rain observatory showed a reflection of an empty laboratory where its own instrument room ought to be. The image appeared only when the glass roof was wet, and vanished whenever the rainfall stopped. {{heroPlayer}}’s observers brought a watering line; {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators held the dry stair beneath the instrument room.

{{hero}} adjusted the roof spray and found a second chamber mirrored behind the rain gauge. The specialist marked its outline on the floor, then heard a voice from below the marked spot asking for the water to stop. The image began fading even though the roof was still wet.

The observers could keep the spray running to hold the chamber’s position, but the water was spilling toward the old electrical panels. The investigators had found a maintenance hatch below. The specialist held the hose while the voice called again, closer to the stair this time.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s observers found the mirrored chamber and reached the voice safely.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators took the hatch and brought its occupant up the dry stair.
endings.draw: The voice was heard, but the chamber’s outline vanished before either party could open it.

paragraphs: A meteorite displayed in a memorial garden began focusing sunlight through a crack in its case. Its bright line pointed toward a locked crypt beneath the far wall. {{heroPlayer}}’s researchers entered from the garden path; {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators guarded the crypt gate, certain the light had moved since morning.

{{hero}} covered a researcher examining the case. Fire struck a stone bench, and the fighter answered while the researcher tilted the meteorite slightly. A second line appeared, revealing the crypt’s old ventilation grate. From behind the grate came a gust of cool air and the smell of fresh paint.

The researchers could preserve the light’s alignment or open the grate to see who had entered the crypt. The investigators had a key to the gate, but the lock looked newly replaced. The fighter watched both lines of sunlight move as the afternoon shade approached the garden wall.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s researchers secured the meteorite and opened the marked grate.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators took the crypt gate and discovered who had changed its lock.
endings.draw: The garden remained safe, but the light faded before the crypt’s second entrance was found.

paragraphs: The leaves of an abandoned treehouse grew back in a pattern matching the footprints beneath it. One trail climbed the trunk and did not return. {{heroPlayer}}’s field observers reached the lower branches; {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators guarded the ladder, where a child’s satchel hung from a rung.

{{hero}} followed the leaf pattern to a hollow in the trunk and found a sealed compartment containing a folded trail map. The specialist opened it just enough to see a path to a second treehouse beyond the fence. A bell rang from that direction, and the living leaves changed their pattern as though someone had moved.

The observers could follow the new trail or keep the map where the leaves might update it again. The investigators had a route through the fence but no view of the second treehouse. The specialist held the map against the trunk while the satchel’s owner called from somewhere above.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s observers traced the living map and found the missing climber.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators secured the ladder and reached the second treehouse.
endings.draw: The satchel was returned, but the leaves hid the new trail before either group could map it.

paragraphs: An automated transit junction began sending every shuttle to the same disused platform. A traveler had boarded one of them before anyone noticed the wrong signs, and their luggage was still aboard. {{heroPlayer}}’s traffic analysts reached the controller; {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators held the platform entrance while the traveler’s family waited nearby.

{{hero}} checked the route table and found a forgotten platform number inserted between two current stops. The specialist corrected it, bringing the traveler’s shuttle back into contact. Then the disused platform’s lights came on and another voice answered over the same channel, asking why no one had arrived.

The analysts could bring the shuttle directly home or route it briefly through the old platform to find the other speaker. The investigators had a guarded stair to the old stop. The specialist watched two arrival times appear on the controller for the same single vehicle.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s analysts returned the traveler and traced the second voice from the controller.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators took the old platform and brought both callers to safety.
endings.draw: The traveler came home, but the old stop stayed lit without an arriving vehicle.

paragraphs: A radio tower began broadcasting directions to a caravan that had gone missing on the plains. The message named a well no current chart showed, along with a warning to bring water. {{heroPlayer}}’s analysts approached its transmitter room; {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators held the outer fence, where fresh wagon ruts crossed the dirt.

{{hero}} covered a technician climbing to the tower console. Fire chipped the concrete beside the door, and the fighter answered while the technician found a route card caught in the feed. It showed the unknown well and a second stop farther south, with a hurried mark beside the caravan’s name.

The analysts could transmit the new route to searchers now or keep the tower listening for another message. The investigators had followed the ruts toward the southern stop. The fighter watched the technician hold the card near the microphone as a faint voice returned to the speaker.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s analysts located the caravan and kept the tower broadcasting its safe route.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators followed the wagon ruts and brought the travelers home.
endings.draw: The route was shared, but both teams lost the signal before reaching the marked well.

paragraphs: A stone bridge carried a pilgrimage over an aqueduct that had recently run dry. An inscription under the parapet named a hidden source in the hills. {{heroPlayer}}’s escort reached the central arch; {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators held the far end, where a pilgrim had found a loose stone.

{{hero}} fought a defender beside the parapet and held them back while a mason lifted the stone. Beneath it lay a small gate key and a sketch of a channel feeding the aqueduct. A pilgrim called that water had begun sounding under the bridge again, though the stone trough was still empty.

The escort could follow the sketch uphill or open the gate beside the bridge to see what was coming. The investigators had the aqueduct’s old survey book at the far end. The fighter held the key as a first thin stream appeared in the dry trough below.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escort found the source and kept the bridge open for the pilgrims.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators secured the gate and restored the aqueduct from its survey.
endings.draw: The water returned, but both parties left the source under joint protection.

paragraphs: A traveling court reached a ferry landing with a sealed evidence trunk. Its case number had been changed while the boat was still on the river. {{heroPlayer}}’s inspectors entered the dock office; {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators guarded the ferry, where the only witness refused to come ashore.

{{hero}} compared the case number to a second mark beneath the trunk’s handle and found an older hearing recorded in the dock ledger. The specialist turned to that page as the witness shouted that someone had opened the office window during the crossing. Wet footprints led from the window toward an unused storage shed.

The inspectors could follow the tracks or keep the trunk beside the witness until its seal was verified. The investigators had eyes on the shed from the ferry. The specialist held the ledger open to the older case as a key turned in the shed’s lock.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s inspectors secured the evidence and identified who changed its number.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators held the ferry and brought the witness through the hearing.
endings.draw: The trunk remained sealed while both parties traced the wet footprints.

paragraphs: A pilot’s distress signal arrived from a reconnaissance drone instead of its aircraft. The drone had landed in an empty schoolyard with its camera pointed at a locked shed. {{heroPlayer}}’s flight detail approached by the fence; {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators held the school doors after children reported hearing someone inside.

{{hero}} covered a mechanic recovering the drone. Fire struck the fence posts, and the fighter answered while the mechanic replayed its final image. The pilot had stood beside the shed only minutes earlier, carrying a bright orange panel. A knock sounded from within as the camera continued recording an empty doorway.

The mechanic could open the shed now or trace the drone’s route to see whether the pilot had left through another gate. The investigators had a key from the school caretaker. The fighter watched the orange panel appear for one frame on the live camera, then vanish behind the shed wall.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s detail found the pilot and secured the drone’s full flight record.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators opened the shed and brought the caller to safety.
endings.draw: The shed was empty when opened, leaving both groups with only the drone’s images.

paragraphs: A miners’ warning lamp lit over a sealed tunnel although the shafts had been abandoned for years. A crowd had gathered at the entrance to ask whether someone was trapped within. {{heroPlayer}}’s engineers brought a portable meter; {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators held a side passage the old plans left unmarked.

{{hero}} checked the lamp circuit and found it powered by a small battery hidden beneath the entrance step. The specialist traced its wire toward the side passage, where fresh dust lay on the floor and a muffled voice named a miner missing long before the shafts closed.

The engineers could open the sealed tunnel or follow the wire into the side passage without telling the crowd what they had heard. The investigators had already placed a lantern at that second entrance. The specialist held the meter against the wall as its needle moved with each whispered word.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s engineers opened a safe route and traced the warning lamp to its source.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators secured the side passage and found who had powered the signal.
endings.draw: The tunnel stayed sealed while both teams kept listening for the voice beneath it.

paragraphs: In a walled orchard, a row of prayer ribbons began twisting toward a path that had been bricked up. A gardener reported a visitor’s footsteps there after the evening bell. {{heroPlayer}}’s custodians came through the east gate; {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators held the arch leading to the old wall.

{{hero}} fought a defender at the narrow arch and kept the path open for a gardener carrying a lantern. The fighter pulled a loose ribbon from the wall and found a key tied at its end. Behind the bricks, a small wind chime sounded and someone called for the orchard gate to stay open.

The custodians could use the key on the wall’s concealed lock or follow the voice around to a service door outside the orchard. The investigators knew that second route. The fighter held the ribbon against the evening wind as a shadow crossed the crack between two bricks.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s custodians opened the old path and found the missing visitor.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators secured the service door and brought the visitor out.
endings.draw: The voice stopped, leaving both groups guarding the newly opened wall.

paragraphs: A clock tower relayed a dispatch by striking its bell in an unfamiliar rhythm. The message seemed to come from an abandoned postal route across the ridge, closed years before the bell was installed. {{heroPlayer}}’s listeners reached the tower floor; {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators held the stair with the old route maps.

{{hero}} covered a signaler climbing toward the bell. Fire struck the clock face, and the fighter answered while the signaler found a small hammer tied to a wire from the attic. The wire led through a broken window toward the ridge, where a distant lamp began flashing in time with the bell.

The listeners could sever the wire to stop the bell or leave it sounding while they followed the lamp. The investigators had a safer descent from the attic and could see the ridge path. The fighter watched the hands of the damaged clock cross midnight as the lamp flashed again.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s listeners traced the dispatch and secured the tower and its signal.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators took the attic and followed the old postal route.
endings.draw: The bell fell silent, but both teams kept the route maps for another search.

paragraphs: Paper boats appeared overnight in a canal beside the municipal garden, each carrying a word from a missing letter. The current led toward a locked waterworks building. {{heroPlayer}}’s guides arrived at the garden landing; {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators held the bridge where the canal passed out of sight.

{{hero}} collected the boats in order and pieced together a warning about a pump below the waterworks. The specialist opened a service chart and found a dry maintenance ledge running along the canal. As they marked it, another boat emerged from the locked building with a fresh word written in wet ink.

The guides could cross the maintenance ledge to the building or keep collecting boats until the full message appeared. The investigators had a key to the bridge gate but no access to the ledge. The specialist held the newest word against the chart as the pump began to thrum under the water.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s guides reached the pump and recovered the complete letter.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators secured the waterworks and traced the boats from the bridge.
endings.draw: The pump stopped safely, but the missing letter remained unfinished in both teams’ hands.

paragraphs: An abandoned weather archive grew a ring of moss around one file cabinet while the rest of the building stayed dry. Its records covered a season when the nearby valley had been evacuated without an explanation. {{heroPlayer}}’s botanists came to examine the growth; {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators guarded the archive door.

{{hero}} lifted a strand and found a fine root leading through the cabinet lock. The specialist opened it to a bundle of maps, one damp and marked with the location of a buried shelter. A fresh drop fell from the ceiling onto the map, though the roof above it had no hole.

The botanists could carry the damp map outside, risking its fragile ink, or follow the root to see whether the shelter was still connected to the archive. The investigators had a dry case ready. The specialist held the map level as another drop fell directly onto the shelter mark.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s botanists preserved the map and found the hidden shelter beneath the valley.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators took the cabinet and secured its weather records.
endings.draw: The map survived, but both parties left the archive’s unexplained water source unopened.

paragraphs: A freight train stopped at a border siding during a lightning storm. Its sealed car held relief blankets, but a dispatch nailed to the door ordered it sent back toward the storm. {{heroPlayer}}’s hired guards reached the siding; {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators occupied the station office with the original route book.

{{hero}} covered a conductor crossing the wet platform. Shots struck the signal board, and the fighter answered while the conductor opened the sealed car. Beneath the blankets lay a small generator already running, its cable leading through the floor to a light beneath the tracks.

The guards could uncouple the car and investigate the light, or move the blankets toward the families waiting inland before the storm worsened. The investigators had located an old underpass on the route book. The fighter watched the hidden light flicker as the train’s engine began to warm.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s guards delivered the blankets and traced the generator’s hidden cable.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators secured the siding and followed the light into the underpass.
endings.draw: The relief cargo stayed safe, but both sides kept the car at the station until the storm passed.

paragraphs: The auctioneer had vanished, leaving a private sale in a fortified counting house and one lot locked beneath the floor. Every bidder wanted the little copper cylinder named on the sale card. {{heroPlayer}}’s escorts arrived with a buyer’s receipt; {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators held the stair where the auctioneer had last been seen.

{{hero}} held the upper gallery while a locksmith lifted the floor plate. A shot shattered the hanging lamps, and the fighter fired at the muzzle flash instead of the retreating figure below. In the darkness the locksmith found the cylinder still attached to a wrist by a fine wire: whoever took it would pull a bell in the basement.

The escorts could cut the wire and leave the auctioneer’s route unexplored, or follow it down with the cylinder still tethered. The investigators heard the bell’s answering chime from beneath their stair. With the buyers shouting outside, the fighter watched the locksmith raise a cutter to the wire.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escorts secured the cylinder and traced the missing auctioneer through the basement.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators reached the bell first and recovered the tethered cylinder.
endings.draw: The cylinder stayed under guard while both parties searched for its missing seller.

paragraphs: At a mountain tollhouse, the gates shut behind a convoy carrying a sealed evacuation roster. Someone had replaced the road signs below with arrows toward an unused quarry. {{heroPlayer}}’s drivers wanted the gate open before darkness; {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts wanted to inspect the roster before another vehicle went through.

{{hero}} fought through the narrow mechanism room to reach a jammed handwheel. The fighter drove a guard back against the stone wall, then leaned into the wheel as the convoy’s lead engine sounded from outside. A folded map fell from the axle housing, showing an alternate route with the names of the roster’s passengers written alongside it.

Raising the barrier would put the convoy on the signed road, where the scouts already had a clear view. The hidden route might keep the passengers out of sight, but nobody knew who had prepared it. The fighter held the wheel while the drivers called for a decision through the gate.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s drivers opened the tollhouse and guided the passengers beyond the false signs.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s scouts took the gate and checked every name before the convoy moved.
endings.draw: The convoy sheltered at the tollhouse while both groups investigated the altered map.

paragraphs: A city’s emergency relay station began announcing an evacuation through streets that had been closed for demolition. Residents followed its voice toward the fenced district. {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians reached the station with an updated route; {{otherPlayer}}’s searchers entered the empty streets to learn who had changed the broadcast.

{{hero}} opened the relay cabinet and found a second transmitter fitted behind the official one. The specialist could cut its power, but a small screen showed the position of a child still walking inside the restricted district. As a patrol approached the cabinet, {{hero}} patched a warning into the public channel without revealing the child’s location.

The false transmitter still carried a signal strong enough to drown the warning. The searchers offered to guide the child out if the technicians kept it alive long enough to trace its origin. Sirens echoed off the empty buildings, and the specialist had seconds to choose which wire to pull.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians corrected the warning and led the child away from the fence.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s searchers secured the district and located the hidden broadcaster.
endings.draw: The child reached safety, but the source of the false evacuation stayed hidden.

paragraphs: A rail museum preserved a carriage with its doors welded shut after a border incident. In the morning, a fresh destination card appeared in its window, bearing the name of a station that had burned down. {{heroPlayer}}’s custodians came to open the carriage; {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators guarded the coupling to keep the exhibits intact.

{{hero}} covered a mechanic as sparks fell from the first cut. Fire came from behind the old ticket barrier, and the fighter held that angle until the mechanic pulled back the door. Inside lay a working route selector and a suitcase tagged for the demolished station, with a train ticket dated for the next morning.

The mechanic wanted to disconnect the selector before anybody tried the carriage’s controls. The investigators recognized the suitcase tag from a passenger inquiry and wanted to leave it undisturbed. A low vibration passed through the still carriage while the fighter held the open door against its spring.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s custodians secured the carriage and identified who had planted the ticket.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s investigators recovered the suitcase and protected its possible owner’s trail.
endings.draw: The carriage was locked again, with the ticket sealed for further examination.

paragraphs: Two harbor watch crews received matching orders to secure an empty pilot house before the tide turned. Each had the same seal, yet one order named the harbor master as missing and the other ordered him detained. {{heroPlayer}}’s crew reached the chart table; {{otherPlayer}}’s crew approached from the pier with the master’s last signed log.

{{hero}} laid the two orders beneath a lamp and spotted a tiny error in the copying of a tide mark. The specialist opened the table drawer to find a third, unsigned chart showing a boat anchored beyond the breakwater. As footsteps sounded on both stairs, {{hero}} rubbed salt from the chart’s edge and uncovered the boat’s call sign.

The harbor master might be aboard that boat or might have planted the chart to draw both crews out. The tide would carry the boat beyond the navigation lights before another launch could be readied. The specialist held the chart between the rival orders and asked the crews for a single working channel.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s watch crew secured the pilot house and contacted the boat beyond the lights.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s watch crew took the charts and reached the harbor master first.
endings.draw: Both crews kept the pilot house open while a launch checked the conflicting orders.

paragraphs: A refrigerated cargo bay held a crate of experimental antidote that had arrived without its temperature record. On the quay, a sick customs officer needed a dose before the sample could be tested. {{heroPlayer}}’s medics entered with a portable assay kit; {{otherPlayer}}’s harbor guards held the crate under seal.

{{hero}} drew a sample through the crate’s inspection port and watched two lines appear where the assay promised only one. The specialist recognized a stabilizer in one vial and a harmless dye in the other, but the crate labels had been switched. As the officer’s breathing worsened outside, {{hero}} matched the stabilizer’s batch mark to a note on the crate’s underside.

Opening the crate would break the guards’ seal, while waiting for authorization would leave the officer without help. The harbor guards offered a witness and a spare camera, enough to preserve an honest record of the choice. The specialist held the correct vial in gloved fingers as the quay clock sounded.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s medics verified the antidote and treated the officer under witnessed seal.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards secured the shipment and found another safe dose through customs.
endings.draw: The officer received care while both teams quarantined the mislabeled crate.

paragraphs: A floating market’s music stage slid away from its moorings during the morning rush, carrying the only working repeater for the district. A child on the stage used it to call for help. {{heroPlayer}}’s ferry crew pushed off in a small boat; {{otherPlayer}}’s harbor officers guarded the closed bridge and watched the current.

{{hero}} held the bow while a deckhand prepared a throw line. Fire cracked from a maintenance barge tucked beneath the bridge, and the fighter drove its gunner back long enough to reach the drifting stage. A new cable beneath the stage snagged the ferry boat; it led back toward the barge, pulling both vessels into the bridge supports.

The deckhand could cut the cable and lose whoever had attached it, or use it to draw near enough for an arrest. The child was still at the repeater, asking when the boat would come alongside. The fighter steadied the bow as the stage bumped once against a stone pier.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s ferry crew freed the stage and brought its passengers ashore.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s harbor officers took the bridge and intercepted the cable’s other end.
endings.draw: The passengers escaped, though the repeater drifted away before either crew recovered it.

paragraphs: During a public festival, a masked performer carried a sealed petition onto the customs balcony and disappeared into the crowd below. The petition’s signers claimed an entire block had been erased from the property register. {{heroPlayer}}’s performers searched behind the parade floats; {{otherPlayer}}’s officers held the balcony doors and the surviving register.

{{hero}} grappled with a pursuer in the cramped frame of a festival float. The fighter forced open its painted hatch, revealing the missing performer crouched with the petition under one arm. Beneath them the float’s axle had cracked; a push from the parade behind would send it into the crowd unless someone set a brake.

The performer could hand over the petition and escape while the others held the wheel, or stay long enough to point out the forged page in the register. The officers on the balcony could see the broken axle and were calling for space. The fighter reached for the brake as drums approached.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s performers stopped the float and brought the forged entry into daylight.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s officers secured the petition and kept the crowd clear of the float.
endings.draw: The parade halted safely, but the disputed block remained off the register.

paragraphs: A salvage diver surfaced with a ceramic compass from a harbor wreck, then refused to return to the water. Its needle pointed toward a dry warehouse instead of north. {{heroPlayer}}’s repair crew brought a portable scanner to the warehouse; {{otherPlayer}}’s harbor patrol sealed the wreck while the diver gave a statement.

{{hero}} traced the compass’s signal through a wall of stacked timber and found an old hull plate welded into the warehouse foundation. The specialist set the scanner against its rivets as a faint tapping came from behind. The map on the screen showed a narrow chamber beneath the floor, built before the warehouse itself.

The repair crew could open the chamber from inside, but water from the tide pressed against its harbor side. The patrol offered a pump if the crew surrendered the compass for evidence. The specialist checked the rising pressure on the scanner and marked a safe opening before the next wave struck.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew opened the chamber and brought its hidden contents above the tide.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol secured the compass and reached the chamber through the wreck.
endings.draw: The chamber stayed sealed while both teams reinforced the flooded foundation.

paragraphs: A contract broker placed a sealed debt ledger in an automated exchange booth and vanished before the other party arrived. The booth began charging each person who tried its door, including people who had never borrowed a credit. {{heroPlayer}}’s auditors came with a court key; {{otherPlayer}}’s port wardens held the queue away from the machine.

{{hero}} accessed the booth’s transaction history and found payments routing to a trust named for a ship lost years earlier. The specialist froze the account, but the booth started printing receipts bearing the names of people waiting outside. One receipt included the broker’s signature and a storage address beneath the old ferry terminal.

The auditors could keep the booth frozen or follow that address before the broker cleared the ledger. The wardens needed the court key to stop the printer from exposing more names. As the queue pressed toward the glass, the specialist reached for a single copy of the earliest receipt.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s auditors stopped the false charges and located the missing broker’s records.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens secured the exchange booth and protected the people in its queue.
endings.draw: The ledger remained frozen, with the trust’s owner still unidentified.

paragraphs: A lifeboat washed into a naval training basin with nobody aboard and every safety light burning. Its emergency transmitter carried a mayday from a ship absent from harbor records. {{heroPlayer}}’s dock watch moved to the boat ramp; {{otherPlayer}}’s search party took cover beside the simulator building where the transmission had first appeared.

{{hero}} held the ramp as a sailor leaned into the empty lifeboat. Fire struck the waterline, and the fighter returned it while the sailor lifted an insulated cover from the floor. Underneath was a live transmitter wired to a model of the training basin, its tiny warning lights marking three real gates along the quay.

One of the gates led out to open water; another was the only way to reach the missing ship’s supposed position. The search party had already moved toward the third. The fighter watched the sailor copy the lights’ pattern as the lifeboat’s mayday changed to a countdown.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s dock watch secured the transmitter and checked all three marked gates.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s search party took the simulator and traced the false mayday.
endings.draw: The countdown ended harmlessly, but the lifeboat’s origin stayed unanswered.

paragraphs: A fortress built from ship ballast guarded a narrow causeway to the old signal fort. Inside its gatehouse lay a brass stamp that could authorize passage through the entire inlet. {{heroPlayer}}’s assault team approached at low tide; {{otherPlayer}}’s keepers barred the gate and hid the stamp among decoys.

{{hero}} forced through a crush of defenders at the gate hinge and held open just enough space for a companion to search. A stone block dropped from above and jammed the gate half open. The companion found the real stamp inside its hollow core, but the returning tide had begun washing through the exposed causeway.

The team could lift the block and withdraw with the stamp or push toward the fort before the crossing vanished. The keepers had a dry passage behind the gatehouse and might reach the signal bell first. The fighter braced against the iron hinge while the companion weighed the heavy stamp.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s team carried the stamp across the causeway and claimed the fort’s gate.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s keepers recovered the stamp and sounded the signal bell.
endings.draw: The tide cut off both groups, leaving the stamp trapped in the gatehouse.

paragraphs: Above a coastal repair yard, a survey satellite began broadcasting images of an inlet that had been drained decades ago. A crew at the yard recognized its own building in the pictures, submerged to the roof. {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians came to retrieve the receiver; {{otherPlayer}}’s dock officers kept workers clear of its antenna.

{{hero}} aligned the receiver by hand and recovered the image’s timestamp: tomorrow morning. The specialist then saw a small maintenance valve in the picture, open against a wall that stood dry beside the yard today. When an officer pointed out a matching valve below the antenna, {{hero}} sent a worker to check its seal.

The valve was intact, but the satellite kept adding water to every new image. The dock officers wanted the receiver disconnected so the workforce would not panic. The technicians needed one last pass to see whether the pictures showed a cause. The specialist held the alignment as clouds crossed the antenna.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians isolated the flood risk and kept the repair yard working.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s officers secured the receiver and evacuated the vulnerable dock.
endings.draw: The yard closed for inspection while both teams tested the stubborn images.

paragraphs: A lighthouse keeper found fresh footprints on the glass stair to a lamp that had been extinguished for years. By dusk the lamp lit again, aimed inland toward a crowded station rather than out to sea. {{heroPlayer}}’s search unit reached the cliff path; {{otherPlayer}}’s harbor watch held the keeper’s cottage and its spare lens.

{{hero}} covered the narrow landing while a climber moved toward the lamp. Shots from the cottage struck the railing, and the fighter answered through the glass without breaking the lens. The climber found a shutter in the housing cut to throw a coded shape over the station’s ticket hall, where passengers had begun to gather beneath it.

Removing the shutter would end the signal, though it might also hide a warning meant for someone at the station. The harbor watch had the spare lens and could change its direction from below. The fighter watched the shadow stretch across the ticket hall as the first train came into view.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s search unit controlled the lamp and decoded the message above the station.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s harbor watch secured the lighthouse and redirected its strange beam.
endings.draw: The lamp went dark before its intended recipient stepped forward.

paragraphs: At a port customs hall, an unclaimed violin case triggered the declaration sensor without containing anything metal. Its owner had signed in and walked out under a different name. {{heroPlayer}}’s examiners reached the inspection table; {{otherPlayer}}’s officers guarded the exits with a still image of the traveler.

{{hero}} opened the case and found a second layer sewn into the lining, thin enough to evade a hurried search. The specialist held it up to the hall light and read a string of berth numbers pressed into the fabric. One number belonged to a vessel leaving before midnight; another was for a ship that had sunk there years ago.

The examiners could follow the living vessel or search the archives for the lost one. The officers knew the traveler’s face but could not agree whether the case had been left as bait. The specialist folded the lining along its creases and found that the two berth numbers occupied the same place.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s examiners traced the berth numbers and found the traveler’s intended handoff.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s officers held the customs hall and intercepted the traveler at departure.
endings.draw: The case remained sealed as the living ship sailed under observation.

paragraphs: The harbor collision archive suddenly displayed a warning for a crash that had not happened. Its chart placed two loaded ferries in the same channel at dawn, with hundreds of passengers expected aboard. {{heroPlayer}}’s analysts came to test the warning; {{otherPlayer}}’s dispatchers held the harbor office and its live traffic board.

{{hero}} reconstructed the forecast from the archive’s damaged records and found a missing buoy hidden in the calculation. The specialist contacted a launch to inspect its coordinates. From the office window, the buoy was still visible, but its light flashed on the wrong rhythm, drawing an approaching ferry toward a shallower channel.

The dispatchers could reroute both ferries at once, at the cost of closing the port, or send the launch to reset the buoy while vessels waited. The analysts needed the archive intact to tell whether other warnings had been altered. The specialist marked the next safe passage across the chart with a pencil.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s analysts corrected the chart and guided both ferries through safely.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s dispatchers secured the office and halted traffic until the buoy was repaired.
endings.draw: Both ferries waited outside the channel while the disputed warning was tested.

paragraphs: A city library’s restoration lab found a catalog card listing a book still being written. Its projected title named a trial scheduled to begin the next day. {{heroPlayer}}’s archivists sought the card’s source; {{otherPlayer}}’s port constables protected the witness due to testify, who had arrived to inspect it in person.

{{hero}} examined the card’s ink beneath a lamp and saw the indent of a second title erased before printing. The specialist fitted the card to the library’s old indexing press and recovered a maker’s mark. From the stacks came the sound of fresh cards falling: each now listed a different account of the witness’s testimony.

The witness could leave with the one verified card or stay until the press revealed who had fed it false records. The constables wanted the library doors locked before the trial notes spread outside. The specialist stood at the press, holding the recovered mark beside a drawer full of possible names.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s archivists identified the counterfeit cards and preserved the witness’s account.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s constables secured the witness and seized the printing press.
endings.draw: The witness reached court, but the maker of the cards remained unknown.

paragraphs: Beneath a seaside amphitheater, a service tunnel opened into a newly discovered room filled with campaign banners. A crowd gathered above for a memorial, unaware the floor over the room had begun to sag. {{heroPlayer}}’s guards entered from the stage trap; {{otherPlayer}}’s port wardens reached the room through a maintenance gate.

{{hero}} drove a defender away from the timber brace supporting the stage and held the narrow entrance for the others. A banner unrolled from the wall, revealing the plan for a second brace hidden beneath the orchestra pit. The fighter shouted the location upward while a companion pulled the first timber back into place.

The guards could evacuate the memorial before opening the sealed chamber, or hold the stage while the wardens searched for the buried support. Footsteps and music continued overhead. The fighter leaned against the shaking brace as a thin line of dust fell across the newly revealed plan.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s guards held the stage and opened the room without endangering the crowd.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s wardens secured the tunnel and led the memorial away from the weak floor.
endings.draw: The ceremony ended outdoors while both parties propped up the buried room.

paragraphs: Two ships arrived with custody papers for the same rescued passenger. One document bore a fresh court seal; the other carried the passenger’s own signature, dated before the rescue. {{heroPlayer}}’s mediators asked to meet the passenger in a neutral waiting room; {{otherPlayer}}’s quay officers held both gangways until the papers could be checked.

{{hero}} compared the documents with the passenger present and noticed that both described a distinctive scar on the wrong hand. The specialist asked the passenger to draw the rescue craft from memory. In its stern was a painted mark matching neither ship, and beneath it a number that pointed to a third berth.

The mediators could send someone to the third berth, but the passenger refused to be left alone with either claimant. The quay officers offered a guarded route through the customs hall. The specialist folded the drawing and kept it where all three parties could see it during the walk.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s mediators protected the passenger and established who filed the false claim.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s quay officers secured the third berth and brought the claimant in for questioning.
endings.draw: The passenger stayed under neutral care while the competing papers were examined.

paragraphs: A launch window opened at a small orbital ferry platform, but its departure clock counted down for a craft still listed in storage. An engineer heard footsteps in the fuel gallery and called for an inspection. {{heroPlayer}}’s response team reached the access bridge; {{otherPlayer}}’s platform guards held the ignition booth and its missing key record.

{{hero}} covered the engineer’s crossing when fire flashed from an equipment bay. The fighter returned it through the grated bridge while the engineer found a portable ignition unit plugged into the stored ferry. The countdown was real; someone had set the launch sequence without clearing the gallery or checking the platform’s personnel list.

The engineer could kill the power at the craft, but the controls needed a minute to discharge. The guards could interrupt the sequence from the booth if they recovered the missing key. The fighter held the bridge while a warning siren brought the last workers out of the fuel gallery.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s response team stopped the launch and cleared the gallery safely.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s guards recovered the key and locked down the ferry platform.
endings.draw: The ferry stayed grounded while both teams investigated the unauthorized countdown.

paragraphs: A tug stalled beneath a port’s underwater traffic relay, leaving three arriving vessels without channel directions. The relay cabinet was supposed to be dry, but bubbles escaped around its service hatch. {{heroPlayer}}’s divers boarded the tug with repair equipment; {{otherPlayer}}’s harbor pilots held the signal tower above and began spacing the ships by hand.

{{hero}} climbed through the submerged hatch and found a cable severed cleanly rather than torn. The specialist joined it with a field splice, then noticed the relay was routing one incoming vessel to a berth listed as abandoned. The vessel’s lights came into view through the murk as {{hero}} sent a warning up the cable.

The divers could restore the normal traffic map or trace the false berth command to the person who entered it. The pilots needed an answer before the largest ship committed to the channel. The specialist held the splice clear of the rising water while the tug’s engine finally turned over.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s divers restored the relay and guided the vessels to safe berths.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s pilots took over the traffic signals and discovered the altered route.
endings.draw: The incoming ships anchored outside while both crews rebuilt the flooded relay.

paragraphs: At a waterfront tea house, an elderly courier set down a lacquered box and died before naming its recipient. Inside was a seal used to settle passage for dozens of displaced families. {{heroPlayer}}’s escorts came for the box; {{otherPlayer}}’s harbor officials held the corridor and demanded the courier’s final instructions.

{{hero}} met an intruder at the tea house’s sliding screen and kept the box out of reach. The fighter pushed the intruder into a narrow storage alcove, where a second seal had been hidden under a floor mat. One was stamped with the courier’s old crest; the other was still warm from its press.

The escorts could move the families with the first seal before anyone challenged it, or stop to prove which mark the courier intended. The officials had a register containing years of his signatures. The fighter stood over both seals as voices from the waiting families rose in the street.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escorts verified the courier’s seal and secured passage for the families.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s officials recovered the box and exposed the freshly pressed forgery.
endings.draw: The families waited at the tea house while both seals went for inspection.

paragraphs: A weather balloon snagged on the roof of an old sea shrine after transmitting the position of a ship that had never entered the bay. The shrine caretaker insisted nobody cut its lines near the fragile tiles. {{heroPlayer}}’s surveyors climbed the back steps; {{otherPlayer}}’s coast watchers waited below with the balloon’s last recorded signal.

{{hero}} loosened the tether without disturbing the roof and retrieved the instrument pod. The specialist found two position records inside: one from the balloon, the other from a transmitter tucked beneath the shrine’s bell. When {{hero}} checked that bell, the caretaker recognized a knot tied in the transmitter’s cord as belonging to a missing fisherman.

The surveyors could follow the older position record at once, but the watchers wanted the fisherman’s last contact traced first. The balloon’s gas was escaping, and its shadow moved slowly across the shrine wall. The specialist copied both coordinates onto the caretaker’s paper map before choosing a route down.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s surveyors traced the hidden signal and found the fisherman’s route.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s coast watchers secured the instruments and searched the reported waters.
endings.draw: The shrine kept the pod while both crews searched separate coordinates.

paragraphs: A floating school archive broke its mooring before its records could be transferred to the new campus. Inside were admissions lists for children due to board the next day. {{heroPlayer}}’s recovery crew launched a skiff toward the drifting building; {{otherPlayer}}’s port patrol held the drawbridge until a safe towline could be rigged.

{{hero}} covered the skiff as a shot came from the archive’s upper window. The fighter struck the shutter and bought time for a teacher to climb aboard. In the office, the teacher discovered a stack of freshly edited lists, each removing the same child’s name; a cut mooring rope lay beside the printing machine.

The crew could secure the records on the moving building or tow the entire archive into the bridge’s protected channel. The patrol warned that a larger vessel was approaching the bend. The fighter watched the teacher hold up an unedited list while the skiff nosed toward the cut rope.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew brought the archive ashore with the original lists intact.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s patrol secured the channel and recovered the altered records.
endings.draw: The archive survived, though the missing child’s records required a wider search.

paragraphs: At an estuary nursery, a new coral strain flourished beneath protective glass while native beds outside turned pale. The caretaker feared the nursery’s pumps were feeding the new growth at the others’ expense. {{heroPlayer}}’s ecologists carried sampling tools to the intake; {{otherPlayer}}’s harbor inspectors kept the sluice closed pending an inspection.

{{hero}} tested the intake and found clean water entering but a nutrient concentrate leaving by an unmarked return pipe. The specialist traced the pipe beneath a visitor walkway to a storage tank bearing a research license that had expired years earlier. Opening the tank valve would stop the flow, but pressure had already built behind it.

The ecologists could drain the tank slowly and risk another tide of concentrate, or ask the inspectors to open the sluice and dilute it. Both choices would change the nursery’s delicate conditions. The specialist held a sample beside the fading native coral as the caretakers waited for an answer.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s ecologists isolated the return pipe and protected the native beds.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s inspectors secured the sluice and traced the expired research license.
endings.draw: The nursery remained closed while both teams monitored the coral’s recovery.

paragraphs: A grain exchange beneath the old fish market held tokens for a winter ration shipment. An accountant reported that someone had used the locked token press after closing. {{heroPlayer}}’s guards reached the market cellar through the ice room; {{otherPlayer}}’s dock agents held the public stair and the day’s legitimate ledger.

{{hero}} wrestled a defender away from the press while a clerk counted fresh brass tokens scattered across the floor. One carried a number belonging to a ship not due until spring. The fighter kept the machine from cycling again as the clerk found a second die fitted below it, ready to stamp the counterfeit cargo as inspected.

The guards could seize both dies and stop the ration shipment while its papers were reviewed. The agents wanted to let the marked cargo move under surveillance and see who collected it. The fighter held the heavy press open while the clerk placed the false token beside the original ledger.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s guards secured the press and protected the ration shipment from fraud.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s agents took the ledger and identified who ordered the counterfeit tokens.
endings.draw: The shipment stayed in port while both teams reconciled the tokens.

paragraphs: A shipyard’s contract drawer yielded three blueprints for the same rescue vessel, each specifying a different hull compartment. Its builders had already cut metal to one of them. {{heroPlayer}}’s inspectors reached the drafting loft with a work stoppage; {{otherPlayer}}’s port engineers stood by the unfinished keel with the approved purchase order.

{{hero}} measured the blueprints against the keel and spotted a missing escape hatch in the version on the builders’ table. The specialist marked its position on the floor below, where a welder uncovered an older compartment already framed into the hull. A small parcel sat inside it, addressed to the ship’s first captain.

The inspectors could open the parcel before construction continued, but the engineers warned that removing it might damage the compartment’s seal. The first captain was coming to the yard that afternoon. The specialist kept the three plans spread out while sparks sounded from the stopped welding line.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s inspectors restored the escape hatch and resolved the conflicting ship plans.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s engineers secured the keel and verified the captain’s sealed parcel.
endings.draw: Construction paused until the captain could examine the hidden compartment.

paragraphs: An underwater dining room began taking on water during a charity meal, though its outer glass showed no crack. The diners had gathered to honor a pilot lost at sea. {{heroPlayer}}’s response crew came down the service stairs; {{otherPlayer}}’s harbor rescuers were already lifting children through the dry kitchen hatch.

{{hero}} held the narrow service entrance when fire came from beyond the empty seating area. The fighter kept the passage clear while a plumber followed the rising water to a drain hidden beneath the memorial table. Inside the drain lay a pilot’s nameplate and a hose running toward a locked maintenance room.

The crew could shut the valve in that room or help the rescuers clear the last diners first. The harbor rescuers had a spare breathing rig but no key to the maintenance door. The fighter watched water climb the table legs while the nameplate slid across the wet floor.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew closed the hidden valve and brought every diner to safety.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s rescuers evacuated the room and traced the hose to its source.
endings.draw: The diners escaped, but the flooded memorial room stayed closed for inspection.

paragraphs: A shelter near the docks listed every bed as occupied, although half its rooms were empty. The intake register showed arrivals from a vessel that had never been cleared to land. {{heroPlayer}}’s caseworkers came to check the missing residents; {{otherPlayer}}’s port officers held the loading courtyard where meals were still being delivered.

{{hero}} compared the meals against the register and found one delivery addressed to the shelter’s locked laundry room. The specialist opened it to discover packed bags with the missing residents’ names, each holding a travel ticket for the same evening. On the wall was a departure time written in chalk and then partly erased.

The caseworkers could warn the people named on the tickets, but nobody knew whether they were hiding or had already left. The officers wanted to hold the courtyard until the delivery driver returned. The specialist laid the tickets beside the unclaimed meals and checked which names appeared on both.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s caseworkers found the missing residents and preserved their travel choices.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s port officers secured the courtyard and questioned the delivery driver.
endings.draw: The shelter stayed open while both teams traced the tickets.

paragraphs: The tidal turbine supplying a dockside district stopped at the height of the evening draw. Its service room displayed normal pressure even as the lights went out. {{heroPlayer}}’s maintenance crew reached the intake tunnel with portable lamps; {{otherPlayer}}’s harbor electricians kept the district’s backup power running from a smaller station.

{{hero}} opened the pressure gauge and found its sensor wired to a recording loop rather than the turbine. The specialist followed the live cable to a submerged inspection grate, where fresh scrape marks crossed the metal. A loose panel behind it held the original readings and a hand-drawn map of the district’s blacked-out streets.

The maintenance crew could pull the grate to restart the turbine, or leave it in place while the electricians checked the mapped streets for an unseen hazard. The backup station was already heating up. The specialist held the false gauge beside the original readings as another block went dark.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s crew restored the turbine and located the reason for the false readings.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s electricians kept the district lit and secured the suspect intake.
endings.draw: The district ran on backup power while both teams examined the tampered gauge.

paragraphs: Two emergency teams reached a desert waystation after its water meter reported a supply that nobody could find. A bus full of travelers was due before sunset. {{heroPlayer}}’s team inspected the cistern roof; {{otherPlayer}}’s team checked the well below, each holding a different signed maintenance order.

{{hero}} measured the cistern’s dry walls and discovered an air pocket behind its outer lining. The specialist tapped a hollow seam and heard water moving far below the apparent floor. A narrow bypass pipe led out toward the neighboring orchard, where a child had been filling buckets from an unfamiliar tap.

The two teams could close the bypass and fill the station for the travelers, but the orchard’s trees might depend on that water. The child said the tap had worked for years without anyone charging for it. The specialist placed both maintenance orders beside the pipe and asked whose map showed the orchard.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s team restored the waystation supply and protected the orchard’s share.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s team secured the well and supplied the arriving travelers.
endings.draw: Both teams rationed the water while the bypass was properly surveyed.

paragraphs: A traveling exhibition set up beside a relief depot with a machine that could print prosthetic fittings on demand. Its first patient had to wait when the machine rejected the depot’s stock as unregistered. {{heroPlayer}}’s road crew brought an alternative printer head; {{otherPlayer}}’s relief staff guarded the original stock and its medical specifications.

{{hero}} protected the workbench as fire came through the exhibition’s mesh screens. The fighter drove the shooter away while a mechanic fitted the replacement head, then found a second spool threaded into the printer. It held a patient’s measurements but named the wrong limb, a mistake that would have ruined the fitting.

The mechanic could correct the spool and print immediately, or stop the whole exhibition until the source of the bad file was found. The waiting patient watched the machine from behind a canvas curtain. The fighter kept the screens in view while the relief staff compared the file against the original prescription.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s road crew corrected the printer and delivered a safe fitting.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s relief staff secured the specifications and uncovered the swapped file.
endings.draw: The patient received another fitting while both crews audited the printer’s records.

paragraphs: A night market’s lantern procession stopped when a projection across the square showed a missing dancer trying to speak. The image repeated without sound and pointed toward a locked costume wagon. {{heroPlayer}}’s performers moved through the stalls; {{otherPlayer}}’s search team kept the market gates open for anyone who needed to leave.

{{hero}} pushed past a guard at the wagon steps and held the narrow doorway while a companion searched the costumes. Beneath a false hem lay a tiny projector and a recording of the dancer naming a date in the future. The fighter heard a knock from under the wagon floor just as the lanterns went dark.

The performers could lift the floor to look for the dancer or play the full recording for the search team to identify the date. The market crowd was pressing in, and the open gates gave a clear way out. The fighter reached for the floor latch as the knock came again.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s performers opened the wagon and found the dancer’s trail.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s search team secured the market and decoded the hidden recording.
endings.draw: The lanterns returned, but the missing dancer’s message remained incomplete.

paragraphs: A small orbital elevator stopped with a sealed research capsule halfway between its ground terminal and transfer platform. The capsule contained a tissue culture needed before the next launch. {{heroPlayer}}’s riggers climbed the service spine; {{otherPlayer}}’s specialists held the ground terminal and monitored the culture’s temperature.

{{hero}} reached the stalled carrier and found a loose counterweight cable whipping near its emergency release. The specialist pinned the cable with a temporary clamp and read a handwritten warning on the capsule: the receiving platform had no sterile chamber ready. Through the carrier window, {{hero}} could see its cooling indicator sliding toward amber.

The riggers could lower the capsule to the ground, where the specialists had a sterile room, or repair the lift and meet the planned launch. The ground team needed the carrier’s brake tested first. The specialist held the clamp while the culture’s remaining cold reserve ticked away on the display.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s riggers recovered the capsule and delivered it to a sterile chamber.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s specialists controlled the terminal and preserved the cooling culture.
endings.draw: The capsule was stabilized in place while both teams prepared a safe transfer.

paragraphs: A mobile pharmacy’s privacy screen began displaying customers’ names and treatment times to everyone waiting outside. An attendant had unplugged the screen, yet it continued from its backup cell. {{heroPlayer}}’s systems auditors entered through the rear delivery flap; {{otherPlayer}}’s care team shielded the waiting patients from the public display.

{{hero}} traced the leak to a receipt printer loaded with a blank roll that was secretly recording every transaction. The specialist removed it and found a previous day’s receipts already printed on the inner layer. Among them was one appointment for a patient who had never reached the pharmacy, marked as completed.

The auditors could wipe the display immediately, but doing so might erase the trail to the missing patient. The care team had a paper schedule and could call that person’s emergency contact. The specialist held the rolled receipts behind the privacy screen while the attendant waited for it to finally go dark.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s auditors stopped the leak and traced the missing appointment.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s care team protected the patients and recovered the paper schedule.
endings.draw: The screen went dark, though the absent patient’s whereabouts remained unknown.

paragraphs: A hillside radio array transmitted a request for rescue in the voice of a geologist who had returned from the field that morning. The geologist insisted she had sent no message. {{heroPlayer}}’s search party followed the signal to a locked antenna hut; {{otherPlayer}}’s relief scouts guarded the road where her expedition had camped.

{{hero}} covered an operator reaching for the hut door. Fire cracked from the rocky slope, and the fighter held the approach while the operator found a second microphone wired beneath the desk. Its recorder contained the geologist’s voice asking for help from inside a fissure whose coordinates matched the expedition’s unused route.

The search party could follow the coordinates immediately, but the relief scouts wanted the geologist to listen to the recording first. She was still down the road with the rest of her team. The fighter watched the operator pack the microphone as another call came through the supposedly dead transmitter.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s search party secured the array and checked the recorded fissure.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s relief scouts protected the geologist and located the hidden microphone.
endings.draw: The radio fell silent while both groups compared the call against expedition records.

paragraphs: A road through a dry canyon held the only portable scanner large enough to check a damaged relief vehicle. The scanner’s bridge had shifted, leaving a line of stranded drivers on both sides. {{heroPlayer}}’s column came from the north; {{otherPlayer}}’s engineers approached from the south with jacks and replacement pins.

{{hero}} forced past a defender at the scanner’s narrow turntable and held its gear housing open for a mechanic. Inside lay a broken pin that looked deliberately filed through. The mechanic could replace it, but the bridge had already moved a finger’s width toward the drop under the weight of the waiting trucks.

The column could move the scanner aside and clear the road, or help the engineers stabilize it before the relief vehicle arrived. Both choices required someone to stand on the shifting turntable. The fighter set a foot against its outer rail while the mechanic slid a new pin into place.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s column steadied the scanner and reopened the canyon road.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s engineers secured the bridge and inspected the damaged relief vehicle.
endings.draw: The road stayed closed while both crews braced the shifting turntable.
