{{hero}} forced past a defender inside the tight store and held its door while a salvager opened the box. Its lamp still worked, casting a coded sequence across the wall. The sequence identified another cave beyond the quarry, one marked on the buyer’s map as sealed after a past rescue mission.

The escorts could carry the box to the buyer, but the searchers wanted its signal read before anyone took it away. The tide would cover the first cave soon. The fighter held the door while the salvager repeated the sequence and the buyer unfolded a map showing a dry route inland.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escorts secured the box and located the second cave.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s searchers verified the claim and traced the coded signal.
endings.draw: The box stayed at the store while both groups compared the maps.

paragraphs: A relief ship submitted an insurance claim for a lost refrigerated case, then its crew found the case at a village dock. The seal was unbroken, but its temperature indicator had reset. {{heroPlayer}}’s inspectors arrived with the ship’s log; {{otherPlayer}}’s search party held the dock and asked the village doctor when the case appeared.

{{hero}} tested the contents through the inspection port and found them stable. The specialist checked the case’s handle for salt deposits and saw a tiny paper tag tied inside it, naming a footpath above the village. The doctor recognized it as the route used to carry medicine during a storm when the dock was closed.

The inspectors could release the medicine now, but the search party wanted to know who had carried it across the footpath. Patients were waiting at the clinic. The specialist recorded the intact seal beside the paper tag while the doctor counted the doses needed before nightfall.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s inspectors verified the medicine and traced its unusual journey.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s search party secured the case and protected the village clinic.
endings.draw: The case was held under cooling while both groups checked the carrier.

paragraphs: A storm shelter beneath a freight station began filling with parcels bearing addresses for buildings long gone. One held a family’s emergency papers still needed for relocation. {{heroPlayer}}’s guards entered the parcel corridor; {{otherPlayer}}’s searchers held the shelter stairs and checked whether anyone remained below.

{{hero}} wrestled a defender away from a narrow parcel chute and kept it open while a carrier reached the paper bundle. Behind it stood an empty cart with a route board for the demolished streets. The carrier recognized its handwritten stops, made by a retired driver who had once delivered supplies during an earlier storm.

The guards could return the family’s papers immediately, but the searchers wanted to contact the retired driver before more parcels arrived. Water was running down the station stair. The fighter held the chute while the carrier read the last stop on the route board, a shelter still open today.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s guards recovered the papers and traced the parcels’ route.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s searchers secured the shelter and reached the retired driver.
endings.draw: The papers stayed dry while both groups mapped the old stops.

paragraphs: A rooftop library for families awaiting housing reopened after its books were moved to an unnamed storage site. New books began appearing on the bare shelves each morning, each carrying a handwritten return date. {{heroPlayer}}’s volunteers checked the roof; {{otherPlayer}}’s searchers held the stair and followed the last delivery cart.

{{hero}} compared the return dates and found they matched the days children from the library had moved into new homes. The specialist followed a colored ribbon in one book down to a neighboring balcony, where a former volunteer had set up a little lending shelf. A note offered to bring the missing books back if someone needed them.

The volunteers could ask for the collection’s return, but the searchers worried the other families still relied on it. The rooftop visitors had already begun borrowing again. The specialist held the note beside the new shelf’s lending list and asked the former volunteer how many books could be shared.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s volunteers restored the rooftop library and shared the collection.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s searchers located the books and protected both lending shelves.
endings.draw: The books circulated between the two roofs while ownership was settled.

paragraphs: An archive bridge between two municipal buildings shook during a document transfer, leaving a wheeled cabinet caught between its doors. Inside were the sole records of a bridge repair across town. {{heroPlayer}}’s guards reached the near end; {{otherPlayer}}’s searchers held the far end and kept staff away from the glass floor.

{{hero}} covered an archivist moving to the cabinet as fire cracked against the bridge frame. The fighter held the passage while the archivist secured a drawer that had come loose. It contained a signed repair order for the archive bridge itself, dated weeks before any visible problem had been reported.

The guards could move the cabinet and evacuate the records, but the searchers wanted the repair order checked against the bridge’s construction log. Another tremor crossed the glass floor. The fighter steadied the archivist as the cabinet wheels rolled toward the joint named in the old order.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s guards recovered the records and cleared the archive bridge.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s searchers secured both ends and traced the earlier repair.
endings.draw: The records stayed protected while engineers inspected the shaking joint.

paragraphs: Two observatory teams received equal claims to a forgotten telescope after its lens began showing a missing star. Both agreed the dark spot was real but disagreed over where to search. {{heroPlayer}}’s observers took the eastern control room; {{otherPlayer}}’s observers held the western dome and prepared an older chart.

{{hero}} aligned both charts and discovered the spot came from a tiny chip in the telescope lens, matching the outline of an island. The specialist projected the chip onto a map and found the island had been renamed after the chart was printed. A research vessel was due to pass it the following morning.

The eastern team could tell the vessel to inspect the island, but the western observers wanted the old name verified before distracting its crew. A second lens showed no chip. The specialist held the island’s two names side by side while the dome turned toward the horizon.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s observers traced the dark spot and contacted the passing vessel.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s observers secured the charts and verified the island’s history.
endings.draw: Both teams kept the telescope trained on the horizon overnight.

paragraphs: A restoration laboratory received a recording of a long-demolished train station’s departure bell. Its timestamp named the next morning, and a former station attendant insisted the bell sounded different. {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians checked the audio bench; {{otherPlayer}}’s archivists held the station model and compared the surviving plans.

{{hero}} isolated a small sound beneath the bell and recognized the rattle of a particular signal lever. The specialist found that lever displayed inside the station model, newly polished on one side. Beneath it lay a ticket stamped with the next morning’s date for a route once departing from the demolished platform.

The technicians could follow the ticket to the replacement terminal, but the archivists wanted the model secured before anything was removed. The attendant said one of the old routes still operated under a different name. The specialist held the ticket beside the lever as its metal rattle sounded again in the recording.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s technicians traced the signal and found the ticket’s current route.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s archivists secured the model and identified the polished lever.
endings.draw: The recording stayed in the lab while both teams checked the terminal.

paragraphs: A research courier carried a sealed capsule across a stone aqueduct when its maintenance gate swung closed. A guide on the far side shouted that the aqueduct’s old drain was about to open. {{heroPlayer}}’s rescuers reached the gate; {{otherPlayer}}’s analysts held the control house and searched its water-level logs.

{{hero}} pushed a defender from the narrow gate and braced it open for the courier. The capsule had lodged in a crack beneath the parapet; the fighter held a line while the courier reached back for it. From below came the sound of the drain turning, though the control house lever remained locked.

The rescuers could bring the courier across without the capsule or wait while the analysts stopped the drain. The guide warned that wet stone would soon become slippery. The fighter kept the line taut as the courier’s hand closed around the capsule and water began moving beneath the arch.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s rescuers brought the courier and capsule safely across.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s analysts stopped the drain and secured the aqueduct controls.
endings.draw: The capsule was held at the gate while the old drain was inspected.

paragraphs: A city published two flood forecasts on the same morning, one calling for evacuation and one for an open market beside the river. Both bore the municipal seal. {{heroPlayer}}’s coordinators reached the planning room; {{otherPlayer}}’s forecasters held the gauge station and gathered fresh measurements before the afternoon tide.

{{hero}} compared the forecasts and found one used a river gauge moved upstream after last year’s bridge repair. The specialist visited its old mounting point and saw a chalk line recording a much higher past flood. A shopkeeper recognized the handwriting of a volunteer who had been trying to warn the market vendors.

The coordinators could close the market immediately, but the forecasters wanted to confirm whether the old chalk mark referred to a rare storm. The tide was already rising. The specialist held both forecasts against the bridge plan while the shopkeeper began calling vendors away from the lowest stalls.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s coordinators issued a clear warning and protected the river market.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s forecasters corrected the gauge and verified the tide risk.
endings.draw: The market delayed opening while the two readings were reconciled.

paragraphs: A station’s navigation classroom projected a distress marker on a live star chart even after its teaching system was switched off. A patrol vessel near the marked coordinates reported calm space. {{heroPlayer}}’s security unit reached the classroom; {{otherPlayer}}’s analysts held the chart controls and checked the projection history.

{{hero}} covered a technician crossing the dark room as shots struck the projector frame. The fighter held the door while the technician discovered a second light source inside a hollow desk. It cast the distress marker through a glass slide etched with a station corridor, where a maintenance hatch had been left ajar.

The security unit could search the corridor, but the analysts wanted the slide preserved to learn who planted it. A teaching group was about to arrive for class. The fighter watched the technician switch off the desk lamp as the marker vanished and footsteps sounded beyond the ajar hatch.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s security unit cleared the corridor and secured the hidden projector.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s analysts traced the slide and protected the classroom.
endings.draw: Class moved elsewhere while both groups examined the maintenance hatch.

paragraphs: A weather buoy washed ashore outside a tunnel construction camp, transmitting pressure readings from deep underground. The tunnel’s own gauges showed nothing unusual, even at the lowest shaft. {{heroPlayer}}’s engineers retrieved the buoy; {{otherPlayer}}’s analysts held the control room and compared its message with the camp’s planned drilling route.

{{hero}} opened the buoy and found a cable spool wound with soil instead of seaweed. The specialist followed its tagged end to a collapsed test shaft, where a crew member had lowered the buoy to send readings through the rock. A voice came up the shaft, asking for the air pump to remain on.

The engineers could pull the crew member up now, but the analysts warned the shaft’s rim needed bracing first. A second worker was still missing from the test team. The specialist held the cable steady as the voice below called out the second worker’s position behind a fallen beam.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s engineers braced the shaft and rescued both workers.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s analysts located the second worker and secured the drilling route.
endings.draw: The air pump stayed on while both crews reinforced the test shaft.

paragraphs: A festival archive exhibited a scroll recording the first bridge built between two villages. One village claimed its final page had been copied incorrectly. {{heroPlayer}}’s guardians reached the display room; {{otherPlayer}}’s historians held the cabinet key and brought a photograph of the scroll made before its restoration.

{{hero}} wrestled a defender away from the narrow exhibit case and held its door while a conservator unrolled the scroll. The last page was genuine, but a thin thread connected it to a hidden fold beneath the wooden roller. That fold carried a drawing of a second bridge, one still visible across the valley.

The guardians could show the fold to the villagers immediately, but the historians wanted the fragile thread preserved until it was documented. Festival visitors were already waiting at the door. The fighter held the case steady while the conservator traced the drawing without touching the ink.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s guardians protected the scroll and found the second bridge.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s historians documented the hidden fold and resolved the copy.
endings.draw: The exhibit stayed closed while both villages examined the new drawing.

paragraphs: A farm’s automated pollination calendar began scheduling work through winter, when its orchard would be bare. The grower suspected a faulty sensor, but one hive had already stirred. {{heroPlayer}}’s naturalists reached the orchard; {{otherPlayer}}’s analysts checked the calendar and compared it with the last three harvests.

{{hero}} examined the waking hive and found a single branch flowering early beneath a warm air vent. The specialist followed the vent to a storage shed where a heater had been left running over a box of dormant seeds. Its lid was marked for another farm across the ridge, whose owner had asked for the box back.

The naturalists could move the hive away from the early blossom, but the analysts wanted to know who had changed the calendar before resetting it. The grower brought an unheated box for the seeds. The specialist held the flowering branch while the hive’s first workers circled back through the cold air.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s naturalists protected the hive and returned the dormant seeds.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s analysts corrected the calendar and traced the warm vent.
endings.draw: The orchard stayed quiet while both groups watched the early bloom.

paragraphs: A public safety drill sent residents toward an evacuation route that ended at a fenced research field. The field gate was closed, but the drill signs pointed straight through it. {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol reached the fence; {{otherPlayer}}’s safety officers held the crowded junction and looked for the person who posted the signs.

{{hero}} covered a guide crossing to the gate as shots struck its warning board. The fighter held the path while the guide found a second map attached behind the sign, directing residents toward an open lane along the field’s edge. A penciled note said the route had changed after a recent excavation uncovered unstable ground.

The patrol could move the crowd to the edge lane, but the officers wanted that ground checked before people entered it. A real alarm had begun sounding from the field station. The fighter watched the guide raise the corrected sign as residents waited under the hot afternoon sun.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol guided the residents through a verified safe lane.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s officers secured the junction and corrected every drill sign.
endings.draw: The residents sheltered nearby while both routes were checked.

paragraphs: A living archive kept a record of an extinct forest in woven stems that grew a new ring each season. This year’s ring formed an open gap with no matching weather record. {{heroPlayer}}’s botanists examined the stems; {{otherPlayer}}’s archivists held the old climate logs and checked the archive’s light cycle.

{{hero}} inspected the open gap and found a single fiber dyed blue beneath the living weave. The specialist traced it to a repair made after a storm, when a caretaker had tied the stems around a hidden paper seed list. One name on the list belonged to a tree still growing in a protected courtyard.

The botanists could retrieve the list and compare it with the courtyard tree, but the archivists warned that untying the fiber might damage the annual ring. The caretaker offered to show the original knot. The specialist held the stem with a soft clamp as the archive lights dimmed for evening.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s botanists preserved the weave and verified the surviving tree.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s archivists secured the seed list and restored the missing ring.
endings.draw: The blue fiber remained in place while the caretaker’s knot was documented.

paragraphs: A mountain research lab promised a trial battery to the caravan that carried its supplies through winter. When the caravan arrived, another party presented a receipt for the same battery. {{heroPlayer}}’s escorts reached the loading platform; {{otherPlayer}}’s analysts held the lab’s inventory cabinet and looked for the original agreement.

{{hero}} pushed a defender away from the narrow freight lift and held it while a driver checked the battery case. Its connectors were made for the caravan’s heater, but a second adapter had been packed inside for an unfamiliar vehicle. A note from the lab’s absent chief asked both claimants to test it together before delivery.

The escorts could take the battery to the caravan, but the analysts warned that the test had not been completed. Snow was falling over the pass, and the caravan needed heat before night. The fighter steadied the lift as the driver placed both adapters beside the chief’s old testing notes.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escorts secured the tested battery and warmed the caravan.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s analysts completed the trial and reconciled the two receipts.
endings.draw: The caravan stayed at the lab while both claimants witnessed the test.

paragraphs: A mapping office insured a survey crew against the loss of its original charts. When a chart vanished, its replacement showed a new road straight through an occupied farmhouse. {{heroPlayer}}’s investigators reached the map vault; {{otherPlayer}}’s surveyors held the field notebooks and contacted the farmer before any contractor saw the new route.

{{hero}} compared the replacement with a tracing left beneath the vault glass and found that the road had been drawn around the farmhouse first. The specialist followed the later erasure to a note folded into the tracing. It requested a route to a nearby well for a family whose path had been blocked by construction.

The investigators could restore the old route immediately, but the surveyors wanted the well access protected too. The farmer came to the office with a photograph of the path before construction began. The specialist laid both versions under the glass and measured room for a shared crossing.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s investigators restored the chart and protected both properties.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s surveyors documented the crossing and secured the missing original.
endings.draw: Work on the road paused while the farmer and family reviewed the route.

paragraphs: A hospital research annex received a crate of old mechanical limbs for restoration. One unit began moving before it was plugged in, tapping a steady rhythm on the packing table. {{heroPlayer}}’s salvage team reached the annex; {{otherPlayer}}’s specialists held the workroom and called the former owner’s family.

{{hero}} shoved a defender back from the narrow workbench and held its loose frame as a technician opened the limb. Inside was a wound spring attached to a tiny photograph. The rhythm stopped when the photograph was removed. It showed the former owner standing beside an inventor whose name was missing from the restoration record.

The salvage team could return the photograph to the family, but the specialists wanted to document the spring before the limb was reassembled. The family was already waiting outside the annex. The fighter kept the frame stable while the technician found a second photograph tucked beneath the spring.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s team secured the limb and restored its owner’s history.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s specialists documented the device and located the inventor.
endings.draw: The unit stayed on the bench while the family examined the photographs.

paragraphs: A public learning center lost access to the files students had created after a new indexing system reorganized the archive. The children’s project concerned an old neighborhood footpath about to be closed. {{heroPlayer}}’s advocates reached the classroom; {{otherPlayer}}’s technicians held the archive server and its backup log.

{{hero}} looked through the remaining paper sketches and found one with a small code the students had chosen for the footpath. The specialist entered it into the system and recovered a folder of interviews with residents who had maintained the path for years. A recording described a hidden step needed when the river rose.

The advocates could submit the interviews to keep the path open, but the technicians wanted its archive restored for all the other projects too. The closure crew would arrive that afternoon. The specialist carried the recovered folder toward the river while the classroom teacher gathered the students’ original sketches.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s advocates preserved the footpath and returned the students’ work.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s technicians restored the archive and located the hidden step.
endings.draw: The path remained open temporarily while every interview was checked.

paragraphs: A rooftop sensor array monitored the safety of the city’s oldest pedestrian bridge. Its screen reported a dangerous vibration while the bridge itself appeared perfectly still. {{heroPlayer}}’s guards reached the sensor tower; {{otherPlayer}}’s analysts held the bridge approaches and asked commuters to use another crossing.

{{hero}} covered a technician climbing the array as shots struck the tower bracing. The fighter held the roof while the technician found a loose panel shaking in the wind above the sensor. Beneath it was a recent maintenance photograph of the bridge, showing a support pin set beside the joint rather than through it.

The guards could secure the array, but the analysts needed the bridge inspected before reopening it. Another gust moved the loose panel against the sensor. The fighter watched the technician strap it down while a bridge worker below reached the joint shown in the photograph.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s guards secured the array and helped repair the bridge support.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s analysts protected commuters and found the displaced pin.
endings.draw: The bridge stayed closed while both the panel and joint were fixed.

paragraphs: Two laboratory teams arrived to study a small machine that sorted stones by an unknown property. Each carried one half of the field notebook that described its discovery. {{heroPlayer}}’s researchers took the testing bench; {{otherPlayer}}’s researchers held the sample cabinet and refused to mix the stones before the notes were compared.

{{hero}} aligned the torn notebook pages and found the machine had been sorting stones by the sound they made when gently struck. The specialist tested a sample from the cabinet and heard a note that matched a recorded chime from a long-closed observatory. Another stone was missing from the tray where it had been set.

The first team could follow the sound to the observatory, but the other researchers wanted the lost stone accounted for before anyone moved the machine. A lab assistant remembered lending it to a nearby school. The specialist kept the halves of the notebook together while the assistant called the teacher.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s team recovered the stone and identified the sorting principle.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s team secured the samples and traced the observatory chime.
endings.draw: The machine remained still while the school returned its borrowed stone.

paragraphs: A cultural archive beneath an aqueduct opened for a community reading just as water began spilling through its roof. A guide remained below to save the first edition of a local history. {{heroPlayer}}’s rescuers entered through the lower courtyard; {{otherPlayer}}’s researchers held the upper valve house and searched for a safe way to stop the flow.

{{hero}} forced a defender away from the archive’s narrow doorway and held it for the guide. Behind a shelf, the fighter found a stone channel directing the leak into a second room filled with old scrolls. The guide carried the first edition beneath a coat while a companion pulled a wooden sluice handle from the wall.

The rescuers could close the sluice immediately, but the researchers warned it might send water back through the crowded courtyard. The reading group was already gathering there. The fighter held the doorway clear while the guide called up which scrolls could still be moved before the roof gave way.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s rescuers cleared the archive and saved the local history.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s researchers controlled the water and protected the courtyard.
endings.draw: The reading moved outdoors while both teams dried the recovered books.

paragraphs: A municipal registry listed a retired teacher as the owner of a school building donated long before their birth. Its planned renovation was due to begin that morning. {{heroPlayer}}’s mediators reached the records office; {{otherPlayer}}’s analysts held the school entrance with the original donation plaque and a set of old photographs.

{{hero}} examined the registry and found the teacher’s name was copied from a scholarship awarded by the original donor. The specialist compared the scholarship date with the plaque and identified the real owner: a neighborhood trust still meeting every month. Its current chair was already inside the school, watching the renovation crew arrive.

The mediators could stop the work and ask the trust for its decision, but the analysts wanted the building’s safety inspection completed before pupils returned. The teacher came to the office carrying the scholarship letter. The specialist laid it beside the registry as the trust chair called from the school.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s mediators restored the trust’s ownership and protected the school.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s analysts secured the building and corrected the registry.
endings.draw: Renovation paused while the trust reviewed the donation documents.

paragraphs: A station research module reported a broken seal on a case of meteor dust. No particles appeared outside the sample room, yet its alarm kept sounding. {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol reached the module; {{otherPlayer}}’s analysts held the lab controls and checked the air filters for any escape.

{{hero}} covered a technician crossing the outer hatch when shots struck the door frame. The fighter held the passage while the technician found the sample case untouched and a second empty case hidden beneath the workbench. Its label matched an earlier shipment that had been sent to a school exhibit on another deck.

The patrol could check the exhibit at once, but the analysts wanted the module cleared before the alarm was silenced. Children were visiting the school display that afternoon. The fighter watched the technician test the empty case as a message came through from the exhibit’s curator.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol secured both cases and protected the school exhibit.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s analysts verified containment and traced the older shipment.
endings.draw: The module stayed sealed while the exhibit’s case was inspected.

paragraphs: A tunnel ventilation test made a line of signal flags on the surface rise in reverse order. The tunnel had been cleared, but one work light still shone deep inside. {{heroPlayer}}’s engineers approached the intake shaft; {{otherPlayer}}’s analysts held the test console and checked which fan had started first.

{{hero}} lowered a pressure probe and found a side duct carrying air toward the abandoned work light. The specialist opened its grille to discover a maintenance kit left beside a fresh footprint. In its lid was a diagram for a short bypass that could keep the tunnel ventilated if the main fan failed.

The engineers could build the bypass before another test, but the analysts wanted the footprint identified in case someone remained below. Rain was moving toward the surface intakes. The specialist set the kit on dry ground while the flags rose again, this time beginning at the correct end.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s engineers restored ventilation and installed the safer bypass.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s analysts located the worker and corrected the fan sequence.
endings.draw: Testing paused while the side duct and footprint were examined.

paragraphs: A hillside pharmacy preserved a notebook of old remedies beside its modern research equipment. During an open day, a page vanished and a visitor began searching the garden for a plant drawn there. {{heroPlayer}}’s guardians followed the visitor; {{otherPlayer}}’s researchers held the pharmacy door and checked which page had been removed.

{{hero}} wrestled a defender away from a narrow garden stair and kept it clear while a gardener reached the visitor. In the visitor’s hand was a photocopy, not the missing original. It showed a plant growing beside an old stone fountain; the fountain had been moved years earlier to another corner of the garden.

The guardians could guide the visitor to the relocated fountain, but the researchers wanted the original page found before anyone gathered specimens. The gardener remembered who moved the stone. The fighter held the stair as the visitor explained that the plant might belong to a relative’s lost garden.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s guardians found the plant and returned the visitor safely.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s researchers recovered the original page and verified the remedy.
endings.draw: The garden remained open while the notebook and fountain history were checked.

paragraphs: A museum terrarium grew moss around a fossil believed to come from a forest lost to fire. Overnight the moss formed a narrow trail toward the terrarium door. {{heroPlayer}}’s naturalists inspected the habitat; {{otherPlayer}}’s analysts held the collection log and checked whether the fossil had ever been moved.

{{hero}} lifted a loose patch of moss and found a line of mineral powder beneath it. The specialist traced the powder to a cracked sample jar stored by the door, whose label named a different forest. The curator recalled combining soil from both sites during an exhibition change and had forgotten to update the log.

The naturalists could replace the soil and let the moss settle, but the analysts wanted the fossil’s origin confirmed before another label was printed. A school group was arriving soon. The specialist set both soil samples beneath a magnifier while the curator prepared to explain the discovery to the children.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s naturalists preserved the moss and identified the correct forest.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s analysts corrected the collection log and verified the fossil.
endings.draw: The exhibit remained unlabeled until the soil samples were compared.

paragraphs: A river clinic received a weather warning that its supply launch had been diverted into a closed channel. The pilot sent no distress call. {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol reached the channel gate; {{otherPlayer}}’s researchers held the clinic pier with a receiving team and studied the warning’s source.

{{hero}} covered a guide crossing the lock as shots struck its wet railing. The fighter held the approach while the guide found the gate’s indicator reversed by a loose cable. Beyond it, the supply launch was safely moored beside a family home, delivering an urgent package for a patient who could not travel to the clinic.

The patrol could open the channel for the launch to continue, but the researchers wanted to know whether the cable would misdirect another boat. The pilot called that the package had been received. The fighter kept watch at the gate while the guide marked the correct channel with a temporary lamp.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s patrol corrected the gate and guided the launch onward.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s researchers secured the pier and repaired the warning system.
endings.draw: The launch waited downstream while both teams checked the lock cable.

paragraphs: A living water filter serving a hill settlement changed color overnight, turning its observation window pale blue. The outlet still passed clean water, but its caretaker closed the tap. {{heroPlayer}}’s biologists reached the filter bed; {{otherPlayer}}’s analysts held a set of samples from before the color change and counted the settlement’s reserve.

{{hero}} examined the filter’s upper layer and found a harmless blue dye carried in by a temporary repair pipe. The specialist traced that pipe to a school garden, where children had used the dye to follow water through their own small irrigation model. Their teacher had no idea the model shared a feed with the filter bed.

The biologists could reroute the repair pipe and reopen the tap, but the analysts wanted repeated tests before the settlement used the water. The reserve was enough for the evening. The specialist held a clear sample beside the blue window while the caretaker prepared a notice for the homes.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s biologists isolated the dye and restored clean water service.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s analysts verified the samples and protected the settlement reserve.
endings.draw: The tap stayed closed briefly while independent tests were completed.

paragraphs: An old signal archive offered a reward for a lost field transmitter found near a border road. A salvage driver arrived with a transmitter bearing the correct mark, but a different frequency dial. {{heroPlayer}}’s escorts reached the archive gate; {{otherPlayer}}’s analysts held the listening room and compared the device with its original service sheet.

{{hero}} pushed a defender away from the narrow gate and kept it open while the driver carried the transmitter inside. Beneath its handle lay a folded message giving the location of a still active relay station. The analysts heard a faint reply on the mismatched dial, one repeating the driver’s name in a steady voice.

The escorts could follow the message to the relay, but the analysts wanted the frequency recorded before the transmitter moved. The driver said no one had known he would bring it there. The fighter held the gate as the device repeated the name once more and then fell silent.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}’s escorts secured the transmitter and reached the active relay.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}’s analysts decoded the reply and protected the archive.
endings.draw: The transmitter remained under guard while its new frequency was traced.

paragraphs: A survey buoy above a crowded shipping lane began transmitting two incompatible ownership records. An ALEPH analysis team traced the contradiction to a sealed maintenance pier, where Druze contractors had arrived with a client's claim and a fast launch. {{heroPlayer}} sought the original log before either record could redirect civilian traffic.

{{hero}} slipped past the contractors' perimeter and opened the buoy's local archive. Its earliest entries showed the same coordinates copied from a vessel that had vanished years before. While Druze fire drove the analysts from the pier, the specialist extracted the timestamp that proved when the forgery began.

The launch's captain offered to carry the archive to safety if both sides would stop shooting. Nobody trusted the offer, but a freighter was already approaching the disputed lane. {{otherPlayer}}'s contractors watched the water as the analyst transmitted a warning that did not depend on either ownership claim.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}'s analysts preserved the original log and cleared the freighter's route.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}'s contractors secured the buoy archive before the analysis team could control its release.
endings.draw: The freighter passed safely while both teams retained different pieces of the disputed archive.

paragraphs: A derelict cargo elevator rose through an evacuated arcology and stopped at floors absent from the building plans. ALEPH analysts followed its signal to find an old data core. Ikari fighters came for the salvage rights, carrying a key taken from the elevator's first operator and little interest in the analysts' warnings.

When the elevator opened onto a narrow service bridge, {{hero}} caught an advancing defender at arm's length and forced a passage through the crush. Inside, a wall display showed a floor occupied by people who had never received the evacuation order. The fighter shouted their location over the open channel.

The analysts could copy the core from below, but only the mercenaries had a route to the occupied floor. {{heroPlayer}}'s squad held the bridge while {{otherPlayer}}'s team tried to keep the elevator from moving again. Somewhere above them, someone pressed the call button twice.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}'s fighters reached the stranded residents and kept the elevator under guard.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}'s analysts secured the core and directed a controlled evacuation from below.
endings.draw: Both teams kept their positions until the last residents crossed the service bridge.

paragraphs: An orbital debris monitor warned of a fragment on course for a district that no longer appeared on current maps. StarCo's contract was to open the district for inspection; an ALEPH team wanted the monitor's raw observations first. Both groups reached the rooftop array as the predicted impact window narrowed.

{{hero}} pinned the array's defenders behind its shielding while a StarCo technician turned the dish by hand. The new angle revealed that the supposed fragment had been broadcasting from inside the abandoned district for weeks. Under fire, the technician sent one clear image of a hidden transmitter to every emergency receiver nearby.

The picture emptied the streets faster than the original warning had. {{otherPlayer}}'s analysts could now triangulate the transmitter, and {{heroPlayer}}'s crew could keep a safe approach open, but each side wanted the first look inside. Above the roof, the dish continued following an object no one could see.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}'s crew held the array long enough to guide the district inspection.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}'s analysts isolated the transmitter and controlled the emergency channel.
endings.draw: The district was cleared while both teams pursued separate traces from the same image.

paragraphs: A glacier observatory started reporting summer temperatures in the middle of a blizzard. White Company escorts had been hired to retrieve its stranded crew, while ALEPH researchers requested the instruments before their records were overwritten. The two parties met at a snowbound antenna that still transmitted a warm, empty room.

{{hero}} reached the observatory's manual recorder through a drift that concealed its entrance. The paper trace showed a heating system switching on and off in a neighboring shelter, not a failure of the weather instruments. A faint knock came from that shelter, too soft for the antenna microphone to catch.

The escorts had the tools to open the shelter; the researchers had the code to stop its failing heater safely. Neither group could work from the other's position. {{heroPlayer}} held the recorder in view while {{otherPlayer}}'s team crossed the ice, and the knocking came again from beneath it.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}'s escorts opened the shelter and brought its occupants out of the storm.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}'s researchers stabilized the heater and preserved the observatory records.
endings.draw: The shelter was opened as both groups secured the instruments against the storm.

paragraphs: Two Phalanx detachments received different orders to recover the same combat memory from a ruined training arena. {{heroPlayer}}'s team knew it as testimony; {{otherPlayer}}'s team had been told it contained a compromised tactical pattern. Their command channels fell silent as the arena projector awakened around them.

{{hero}} met an opposing fighter among shifting holographic walls and held the passage in a close fight. Between projected blows, a recorded voice repeated a request for rescue, not a battle command. The fighter broke from the contest just long enough to show both squads the memory's unedited opening.

The request named a real evacuation site beyond the arena, though neither detachment could verify how old it was. The projector began deleting its own frames. One squad guarded the archive, the other called for transport, and the fighter stood between them as the last clear voice faded.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}'s detachment secured the intact memory and sent a rescue team to its coordinates.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}'s detachment contained the archive and verified the evacuation request through command.
endings.draw: Each detachment left with part of the recording and the same unanswered distress call.

paragraphs: An O-12 investigator arrived to seal a damaged field recorder before testimony from a border clash could be altered. Phalanx veterans guarded the recorder's carrier, who insisted the file also held directions to missing comrades. Neither order mentioned the civilians sheltering beside the exchange point.

{{hero}} opened a protected evidence channel while shots struck the recorder's case. The first seconds of audio placed the missing patrol beyond a collapsed transit arch; the rest remained encrypted. The investigator copied the location to the veterans without surrendering the original file or revealing the carrier's identity.

{{heroPlayer}}'s team prepared a chain of custody as {{otherPlayer}}'s fighters cleared a route toward the arch. The carrier stayed with the civilians and asked whether anyone would return. The investigator could offer no promise, only a duplicate map and a channel that would remain open.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}'s investigators secured the recorder and kept the rescue channel open.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}'s veterans reached the transit arch with the evidence needed to find their patrol.
endings.draw: The original recording remained sealed while both teams coordinated the search.

paragraphs: A customs cutter drifted into a crowded orbital berth with its crew sealed behind a jammed hatch. Starmada officers moved to secure the berth; Phalanx troops approached from a rescue shuttle with a different docking authorization. A false distress signal began moving between the ships as they argued over the safe corridor.

{{hero}} fired across the cargo gantry to stop an armed intruder from reaching the cutter's emergency release. The shots gave a Starmada engineer enough cover to isolate the signal repeater. Behind the hatch, a crew member tapped a count of people still breathing, then added one more tap than the manifest allowed.

The cutter's atmosphere was stable for the moment, but its undocumented passenger made every access order uncertain. {{heroPlayer}}'s officers held the gantry while {{otherPlayer}}'s veterans moved a rescue shield into place. The engineer waited for both teams to acknowledge the same count before opening anything.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}'s officers secured the berth and opened the cutter under their rescue protocol.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}'s veterans reached the sealed crew first and protected the unknown passenger.
endings.draw: Both teams guarded the hatch while the engineer verified every person behind it.

paragraphs: A frontier settlement's emergency beacon broadcast a route through a canyon that no longer existed on recent surveys. Torchlight scouts were searching for the missing convoy; Phalanx fighters had orders to secure an ancient relay above the canyon. Dust hid the road until a second beacon flashed from below the cliff.

{{hero}} scaled down to the relay's maintenance panel and found its map had been reversed after a rockslide. The specialist patched a fresh route into the convoy's receiver while the scouts marked safe ground. Above them, the Phalanx guard held off fire from a ridge neither patrol had occupied.

The convoy answered, then cut its transmission as it entered the dust. {{heroPlayer}}'s scouts could follow the new route; {{otherPlayer}}'s guard could keep the ridge watched. Neither had a clear view of the trucks, so they listened for engines between gusts and counted each one aloud.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}'s scouts guided the convoy out by the corrected canyon route.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}'s fighters held the relay and kept the ridge clear for the convoy.
endings.draw: The convoy emerged from the dust while both patrols maintained their positions.

paragraphs: A shrine keeper reported that an archive bell rang every night without its striker. Japanese secessionist scouts arrived to protect the records kept beneath it; Phalanx veterans sought a courier last seen at the same site. The bell rang again as both patrols entered a courtyard lit only by paper lanterns.

{{hero}} stopped an advancing fighter in a close struggle beside the bell's frame. A second strike sounded beneath their feet, revealing a service chamber and a frightened courier using the bell's cable as a signal. The scout moved the fight away from the trapdoor and called the chamber's position to both patrols.

The courier carried a sealed message for someone outside the shrine, but refused to hand it to either armed group. {{heroPlayer}}'s scouts offered shelter; {{otherPlayer}}'s veterans offered a guarded exit. The keeper opened the trapdoor herself, and the bell finally fell silent above them.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}'s scouts escorted the courier and protected the shrine archive.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}'s veterans secured the courier's route beyond the courtyard.
endings.draw: The courier left the chamber under the keeper's protection as both patrols withdrew.

paragraphs: A coastal surveillance station kept tagging ordinary fishing boats as military targets. An Oban reconnaissance cell was sent to recover the station's targeting record; Phalanx troops approached to disconnect its uplink before anyone acted on it. Fog obscured the harbor, and the next tagged boat was already coming home.

{{hero}} entered the station through its flooded maintenance shaft and copied the target list. Every false tag began after a firmware update delivered from an unmanned buoy offshore. The specialist disabled the outbound alarm, leaving the Phalanx guard a short window to warn the boat without exposing its position.

The harbor pilot acknowledged the warning and steered toward a channel both teams could see. {{heroPlayer}}'s cell still wanted the buoy; {{otherPlayer}}'s troops wanted the uplink destroyed. The specialist watched the target list refresh once more, now naming the station itself as the next contact.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}'s cell preserved the targeting record and traced the compromised buoy.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}'s troops silenced the uplink before it could mark another boat.
endings.draw: The fishing boat entered harbor while both teams isolated the station from the buoy.

paragraphs: A fast coastal craft vanished from radar during an eclipse, leaving its navigation light moving across the water without a hull beneath it. Shindenbutai scouts reached the last visible marker by boat; Phalanx veterans descended on the nearby breakwater. Both patrols saw the light reverse direction against the current.

{{hero}} drove a hidden gun position away from the marker while the scouts pulled an injured navigator from the water. The light belonged to a detached guidance drone, still following the course of the missing craft. The navigator pointed beneath the breakwater, where a submerged hatch had swallowed its wake.

The veteran guard could force the hatch, but opening it might flood the chamber beyond. {{heroPlayer}}'s scouts held the marker while {{otherPlayer}}'s team lowered a sensor through the water. The navigator listened for the crew against the stone and heard three deliberate knocks from below.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}'s scouts secured the marker and guided the trapped crew toward an exit.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}'s veterans opened the submerged access and protected the rescue.
endings.draw: Both patrols kept the chamber stable until the missing crew could be reached.

paragraphs: A living memorial garden began growing unfamiliar flowers around the names of refugees whose route had been erased. A Tohaa delegation came to read the change in its roots; Phalanx veterans arrived with an old transport manifest. The two records disagreed about who had ever reached the settlement.

{{hero}} traced the new growth to a sealed irrigation line beneath a memorial wall. Its water carried a chemical marker from a transport hold, preserved for years in the soil. The specialist marked the line for sampling while a Phalanx guard kept the crowded path clear for families arriving to see the names.

The manifest could identify a vessel, but the garden could only show where its water had gone. {{heroPlayer}}'s delegation asked the families before taking a sample; {{otherPlayer}}'s veterans offered to hold the wall open until everyone had read it. A child found one unmarked space and placed a flower there.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}'s delegation preserved the living trace and reopened the search for the refugees.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}'s veterans secured the manifest and identified the transport's last route.
endings.draw: The families kept the memorial open while both records were examined together.

paragraphs: A mining platform's oxygen reserve fell although every shaft was sealed for a holiday. Dashat guards had been paid to protect the payroll office; Phalanx troops answered a workers' emergency call. When the platform lights came on, each floor displayed a different amount of air remaining.

{{hero}} held a narrow gantry against attackers while a guard crossed to the manual valve board. Behind its cover, the guard found a second line feeding an unregistered refuge beneath the payroll office. The workers had been hiding people there, and the automated reserve count had never included them.

The valve could send air down at once, but it would expose the refuge to whoever controlled the platform. {{heroPlayer}}'s guards watched the office door; {{otherPlayer}}'s veterans protected the stairwell. A voice from the hidden level asked for a count, and the guard answered honestly.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}'s guards secured the valve board and restored air to the refuge.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}'s veterans held the stairwell and evacuated the hidden occupants.
endings.draw: The reserve was shared between the shafts while both teams guarded the refuge.

paragraphs: A broker promised to auction the location of a missing Phalanx field hospital from a crowded orbital concourse. Druze security held the auction room under contract, and a Phalanx patrol entered before the bidding began. The broker's screen displayed a countdown instead of a location, drawing frightened buyers toward the exits.

{{hero}} wrestled an armed guard away from the control desk and held the door while a veteran examined the countdown. It marked the time until the hospital's emergency transmitter would exhaust its power. The broker had sold a rescue window as though it were a secret worth owning.

The Druze captain ordered the room sealed until the contract could be read, but the veteran had already transmitted the hospital's last signal to an open rescue channel. {{heroPlayer}}'s fighters held the desk; {{otherPlayer}}'s guards controlled the concourse. The countdown continued for everyone to see.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}'s patrol held the auction room and sent rescuers toward the hospital.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}'s guards secured the concourse and controlled access to the broker's signal.
endings.draw: The rescue channel stayed open while both teams prevented another bid.

paragraphs: A maglev train stopped in an empty tunnel, though its passengers could see daylight reflected in the windows. Ikari fighters held the service entrance under a salvage contract; Phalanx veterans approached from the far platform to find the stalled conductor. The reflected daylight shifted whenever the tunnel power surged.

{{hero}} covered the platform as a veteran crossed to the train's emergency panel. Gunfire forced the Ikari sentries behind a cable drum, and the panel revealed a maintenance mirror left across the light shaft. Its mounting had fallen onto the power feed, trapping the conductor between live sections of rail.

The passengers could walk out if the feed stayed isolated long enough. {{heroPlayer}}'s veterans held one end of the tunnel while {{otherPlayer}}'s fighters guarded the other. Between them, the conductor stepped off the train with a lantern and waved its beam against the false daylight.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}'s veterans held the feed isolated until the passengers left the train.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}'s fighters secured the service entrance and led the passengers out.
endings.draw: The last passenger reached the platform before the tunnel power returned.

paragraphs: A broadcast studio sent an evacuation notice to a district outside any official hazard zone. StarCo had been hired to protect the announcer; Phalanx troops followed a suspected saboteur to the studio roof. The notice was still airing when both teams found the building's emergency transmitter operating without its staff.

{{hero}} isolated the studio's incoming feed and found the warning originated from a small shelter across the district. Its occupants had borrowed the transmitter to request help after losing their own link. The specialist kept their message on the air while removing the false hazard code that had emptied nearby streets.

The announcer returned to find an audience gathered below the studio, waiting for an explanation. {{heroPlayer}}'s crew guarded the broadcast desk; {{otherPlayer}}'s veterans followed the shelter's signal. The specialist handed the microphone to the announcer, who asked the shelter to say exactly what it needed.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}'s crew kept the shelter's call on the air and corrected the district warning.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}'s veterans reached the shelter and secured its occupants.
endings.draw: The corrected broadcast guided help to the shelter while both teams held their posts.

paragraphs: On an icebound border bridge, traffic drones began leading freight convoys toward a missing section of road. White Company escorts stopped the nearest trucks, while Phalanx veterans searched the far control tower. A drone returned alone with a child's scarf caught in its wheel, bringing both patrols onto the bridge.

{{hero}} held a clear firing lane against an armed figure at the tower window while an escort pulled the drone to safety. Its route memory showed the child had crossed to a maintenance hut before the bridge failure. The scarf had been tied to the drone deliberately as a signal.

A convoy sounded its horn behind the escorts, demanding room to turn. {{heroPlayer}}'s guards could protect the approach; {{otherPlayer}}'s veterans could reach the hut. The fighter lowered the weapon only when a small hand appeared at the frozen window across the gap.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}'s escorts stopped the convoy and held a safe route to the hut.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}'s veterans reached the child and secured the broken span.
endings.draw: The child crossed to safety while both patrols kept traffic off the bridge.

paragraphs: Two O-12 teams arrived at a sealed diplomatic archive with warrants signed an hour apart. {{heroPlayer}}'s officers sought a missing witness statement; {{otherPlayer}}'s officers had orders to protect the witness's identity. The archive's entry system recognized both authorizations and would honor only the first one scanned.

{{hero}} found a maintenance terminal and placed the contradictory warrants side by side in its audit log. The older order proved the witness had requested protection before anyone sought the statement. Rather than open the sealed file, the specialist transmitted the conflict to an independent magistrate and froze the terminal's access queue.

Both teams could still hold the archive, but neither could claim the other had arrived without authority. A quiet voice came from inside the sealed interview room, asking whether the magistrate had received the request. The specialist showed the delivery receipt through the glass and waited with both patrols.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}'s officers secured the audit log and preserved the witness statement for review.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}'s officers protected the witness and kept the sealed interview room under guard.
endings.draw: The archive stayed sealed until the magistrate could hear both teams.

paragraphs: A navy courier docked with a container whose manifest described empty space. O-12 investigators held a warrant for its contents; Starmada officers controlled the pier and suspected the seal concealed a hazard. A dockworker heard something moving inside and asked both groups to stand clear of the loading crane.

{{hero}} forced an armed intruder back from the crane controls in a close struggle, leaving the container suspended above a marked safety zone. Through a small inspection port, the officers saw a repair drone repeatedly tapping its broken arm against the wall. Someone had hidden a distress transmitter inside its chassis.

The investigators wanted to preserve the drone as evidence, while the officers needed to lower it before the crane lost power. {{heroPlayer}}'s team guarded the controls; {{otherPlayer}}'s team prepared a sealed examination bay. The dockworker kept watch for another tap and heard one from a different container.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}'s officers lowered the container safely and secured the pier.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}'s investigators preserved the drone and traced its hidden transmitter.
endings.draw: The first container reached the examination bay as both teams searched the remaining cargo.

paragraphs: A frontier settlement received an official map that placed its clinic inside a restricted survey area. O-12 inspectors came to verify the coordinates; Torchlight scouts came with patients who needed the road kept open. The map's boundary moved overnight, cutting through the clinic door by morning.

{{hero}} compared the survey beacon's position with marks left by the clinic's builders. The beacon had shifted on unstable ground, carrying its digital boundary with it. The specialist sent the old and new coordinates to both patrols while the patients crossed the road the map still called closed.

A new boundary required an official correction, but the clinic could not wait for a hearing. {{heroPlayer}}'s scouts placed temporary markers around the safe approach; {{otherPlayer}}'s inspectors recorded each mark for review. From the clinic window, a patient watched the beacon lean another fraction toward the valley.

endings.heroWins: {{heroPlayer}}'s scouts kept the clinic road open and established a safe approach.
endings.heroLoses: {{otherPlayer}}'s inspectors corrected the survey record and secured the disputed boundary.
endings.draw: The clinic remained accessible while both teams documented the moving beacon.
